title: Rice panicle detection from unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery via image restoration and pseudo-depth prior
authors: PAN Pan; Haochun Li; MingXia Li; MINGXIA LI; MINGXIA LI; Guoping Yu; Guo Zhihao; Guoping Yu; Long Yi; Maomao Li; Maomao Li; Guomin Zhou; Jianhua Zhang
abstract: Accurate rice panicle detection using Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) imagery is a key prerequisite for automated counting and yield-related phenotyping. However, existing detection methods generally assume clear input imagery and rely primarily on two-dimensional RGB appearance, making them vulnerable to motion-induced texture degradation and the strong visual similarity between rice panicles and background foliage in dense canopies. To address these limitations, we propose a novel framework for rice panicle detection via image restoration and pseudo-depth prior fusion. First, we introduce the Spectral-Geometric State Space Network (SG-SSN) to explicitly recover task-relevant high-frequency textures from the temporally accumulated blur commonly generated during UAV cruising. Second, we utilize the Depth Anything V2 vision foundation model to infer pixel-aligned pseudo-depth maps from the deblurred images, providing complementary relative geometric cues. Finally, these dual representations are processed by our proposed Rice Panicle Detection with Pseudo-Depth (RPDet-PD) model, which leverages hierarchical pseudo-depth fusion and frequency-spatial structure preservation to achieve precise panicle localization. Evaluations on a large-scale, multi-site, and multi-variety UAV field dataset show that SG-SSN achieves a PSNR of 32.19 dB on a synthetic temporal-accumulation restoration benchmark. Furthermore, the complete cascaded pipeline utilizing RPDet-PD achieves a mean average precision (mAP@0.5) of 91.6 % under the evaluated field conditions, outperforming the evaluated baseline methods. The experimental results indicate that the proposed cascaded framework provides a feasible approach for rice panicle detection under complex field conditions.

title: ANT Model and Graph Digestion: Bottleneck-Guided Whole-Object Compression, Reconstruction, and Fortification
authors: Artiom Kovnatsky
source_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This record separates model and graph digestion into a standalone ANT research track. It treats a neural model or graph as a typed causal multigraph rather than an unordered collection of tensors or edges. Fast structural bottleneck detection proposes candidate regions; Ariadne threads combine message flow, calibration ablation, rare-case Sentinel interventions, structural geometry, uncertainty, reuse, and execution cost; atomic multi-site bites preserve connected or hypergraph functional motifs; motif and Queen codebooks support reconstruction; and graph fortification is formulated as a named-shock inverse problem. The package includes a standalone preprint, source code, the supplied measured graph-bottleneck library, five-seed raw and aggregate results, result matrices, figures, publication prompts, and the four prior graph notes that motivate the design constraints. The new controlled experiment uses six repeated graph modules, three common useful routes, two rare Sentinel routes, and one deliberately misleading high-message structural dead end. The structural cascade flags all 11 cross-module edges, demonstrating that detection alone does not solve selection. Ariadne whole-route digestion matches the planted functional oracle in all five seeds: zero median test and Sentinel MSE, all five useful route groups complete, the rare route preserved, and no decoy selected. Attention-only, calibration-only, curvature-only, and local edgewise selectors select the decoy and lose a rare route. Lossless motif-codebook reconstruction recovers the exact 155-edge graph and degree sequence at an explicitly accounted 6.04× structural description reduction. After attacking the rare route, named-shock Ariadne repair achieves median test MSE 4.57e-7, compared with 1.93e-5 for a curvature proxy and 1.47e-4 for Ghosh–Boyd. Ghosh–Boyd nevertheless produces the largest algebraic connectivity, showing that topology-only robustness and named functional recovery are different objectives. The evidence is synthetic and deliberately scoped. The record does not claim superiority on arbitrary real graphs, a directed-curvature guarantee, successful compression of a medium or large language model, hardware acceleration, or automatic Taleb-style antifragility. The included staged programme proceeds from planted graph truth to small graph/model co-digestion, a medium open model with teacher-unloaded `.antcolony` execution, and only then a renewed 3B-model experiment. «Не сжимать отдельные числа. Обнаруживать, поедать, восстанавливать и укреплять целостные функциональные организмы» «Не награждай модель за ускорение, достигнутое ценой ошибки.» «Не награждай представление за малый размер, если оно перестало быть teacher.» S.V.E. title: ANT 3.0: Angular-Norm Transport, Verified Whole-Object Digestion, and Living Colony Computation [CPU-First]
authors: Artiom Kovnatsky
source_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: ANT is not a new Taylor expansion. It is a mobile, route-aware and reliability-gated architecture for transporting and materializing local Taylor approximants. ANT является единым агентным протоколом для измерения, разделения, маршрутизации, проверки, реконструкции и сохранения информации в нейронных системах. ANT 3.0 is an integrated research release on representing learning, routing, compression, persistent memory, and verified model transformation as the movement of finite-lifetime, provenance-carrying information agents. The framework begins with an exact angular/log-norm reparameterization of nonzero vectors and develops shared residual fields, scouts and harvesters, manifold transport, shortcut mosaics, sparse trail memories, spectral/native codecs, tangent-bundle route programs, and Queen codebooks of reusable generators. The v3.0 extension treats neural networks and graphs as typed causal multigraphs whose digestible units are whole functional organs rather than isolated tensors. Candidate detectors based on attention, activations, graph bottlenecks, curvature, or gradients are separated by a detection/selection firewall from causal auditors, atomic multi-site bite planners, rare/OOD Sentinels, named-shock fortifiers, and deterministic `.antcolony` serialization. A candidate is accepted only when it satisfies a declared quality contract together with real byte and latency accounting, checksum validation, and teacher-unloaded replay. Measured additions include: (i) a five-seed whole-organism Digits experiment with median 7.83× storage reduction and 1.86× measured speedup while preserving a rare subgroup that attention-only selection destroys; (ii) a planted shared rank-32 Queen runtime with 13.62–13.68× measured speedup when the native law exists; (iii) graph experiments separating bottleneck detection from functional selection, reconstructing repeated modules exactly at 6.04× transparent description reduction, and showing that maximizing algebraic connectivity need not repair a named rare function; and (iv) a 50-seed living-colony search experiment with an 88/10/2 risk prior, four-ant squads, decaying Historian memory, creator-built multi-site worlds, a budgeted private Queen gate, and a sealed final audit. Squads plus Historian recover the planted atomic synergy in all seeds, while more adaptive exploration is marginally worse than the fixed squad policy on this family. The release preserves negative results. The earlier Qwen2.5-3B pilot shows that independent aggressive low-rank replacement can produce apparent speedups while destroying perplexity and top-1 fidelity. The included Stage-III Qwen runner is therefore infrastructure and a self-tested protocol, not evidence of a successful large-language-model compression result. Likewise, the living-colony experiment is synthetic and does not establish a universal 88/10/2 optimum or mathematical antifragility. The package contains the 78-page PDF, full LaTeX source, all figures, reproducible code and raw results for the new experiment, a Stage-III Qwen runner, claims and limits, public-run status, study prompts, checksums, and prior companion experiment archives. title: ANT Model and Graph Digestion: Bottleneck-Guided Whole-Object Compression, Reconstruction, and Fortification
authors: Artiom Kovnatsky
source_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This record separates model and graph digestion into a standalone ANT research track. It treats a neural model or graph as a typed causal multigraph rather than an unordered collection of tensors or edges. Fast structural bottleneck detection proposes candidate regions; Ariadne threads combine message flow, calibration ablation, rare-case Sentinel interventions, structural geometry, uncertainty, reuse, and execution cost; atomic multi-site bites preserve connected or hypergraph functional motifs; motif and Queen codebooks support reconstruction; and graph fortification is formulated as a named-shock inverse problem. The package includes a standalone preprint, source code, the supplied measured graph-bottleneck library, five-seed raw and aggregate results, result matrices, figures, publication prompts, and the four prior graph notes that motivate the design constraints. The new controlled experiment uses six repeated graph modules, three common useful routes, two rare Sentinel routes, and one deliberately misleading high-message structural dead end. The structural cascade flags all 11 cross-module edges, demonstrating that detection alone does not solve selection. Ariadne whole-route digestion matches the planted functional oracle in all five seeds: zero median test and Sentinel MSE, all five useful route groups complete, the rare route preserved, and no decoy selected. Attention-only, calibration-only, curvature-only, and local edgewise selectors select the decoy and lose a rare route. Lossless motif-codebook reconstruction recovers the exact 155-edge graph and degree sequence at an explicitly accounted 6.04× structural description reduction. After attacking the rare route, named-shock Ariadne repair achieves median test MSE 4.57e-7, compared with 1.93e-5 for a curvature proxy and 1.47e-4 for Ghosh–Boyd. Ghosh–Boyd nevertheless produces the largest algebraic connectivity, showing that topology-only robustness and named functional recovery are different objectives. The evidence is synthetic and deliberately scoped. The record does not claim superiority on arbitrary real graphs, a directed-curvature guarantee, successful compression of a medium or large language model, hardware acceleration, or automatic Taleb-style antifragility. The included staged programme proceeds from planted graph truth to small graph/model co-digestion, a medium open model with teacher-unloaded `.antcolony` execution, and only then a renewed 3B-model experiment. «Не сжимать отдельные числа. Обнаруживать, поедать, восстанавливать и укреплять целостные функциональные организмы» «Не награждай модель за ускорение, достигнутое ценой ошибки.» «Не награждай представление за малый размер, если оно перестало быть teacher.» S.V.E. title: The Bottleneck has Moved
authors: Jesper Karlsson
source_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Abstract Development capacity is no longer scarce; judgment and accountability are. Organizations still structured around capacity scarcity—backlogs, sprint planning, resource allocation—are optimizing for a constraint that no longer exists. The Bottleneck Has Moved is a discussion paper proposing a thought experiment for organizational design in the age of generative AI and autonomous software agents. It introduces a cross-framework accountability layer (a "plugin") designed to sit on top of existing enterprise frameworks—such as SAFe, Scrum, LeSS, or Kanban—without disrupting higher-level strategic cadences, reporting structures, or desk arrangements. Key Themes & Highlights The One-Human Agentic Team: Reorganizing work around single-human Product Owners backed by multi-agent software casts, ensuring clear, non-delegable single-point accountability. Framework Compatibility: A detailed compatibility matrix mapping how the plugin sits on top of SAFe, Scrum, LeSS, and Kanban. Boundary Conditions & Domain Fit: An explicit analysis of where the model succeeds (edges, digital channels, greenfield) versus where it degrades (highly regulated, tightly-coupled core legacy systems). The Inverted Portfolio Gate: Replacing pre-planned backlogs with a Retrospective Portfolio Showcase, shifting executive decisions from pre-commitment estimates to funding demonstrated, working software (Adoption Decisions). Relocating Product Ownership: Re-anchoring traditional PO capabilities into strategic, load-bearing roles—Portfolio Curator, Demand Router, and Governance Advisor. Open Design Questions: An open examination of operational preconditions, including architectural consistency mechanisms, rubber-stamping risks under 10x volume, developer identity shifts, and maintaining social cohesion.

title: GenAI and LLM-Based Agents in Production and Operations Management: A Systematic Review
authors: Ömür Demirer
abstract: This systematic review examines how generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and large language model (LLM)-based agents are applied across the operations management (OM) decision spectrum, including demand forecasting, capacity planning, production planning and scheduling, inventory management, quality control, maintenance planning, workforce and operator support, supply chain and logistics, lean and agile production, and product design and technology selection. Prior reviews of AI in operations management have targeted classical AI paradigms. The most recent and comprehensive of these (Martuscelli et al., 2026, Production Planning & Control) synthesised 67 studies but restricted its search terms to "artificial intelligence", "machine learning", "deep learning", "neural network", and "natural language processing", excluding "large language model", "generative AI", and related terms; consequently only one study in that corpus concerned LLM use. Generative systems constitute a distinct technological class, introducing natural-language interfaces, model and formulation generation, external tool invocation (solvers, simulators, MES/ERP systems), and varying degrees of autonomous action. Since 2024 a rapidly growing primary literature has applied these capabilities to core production management decisions, yet this evidence remains unsynthesised. The review makes three contributions. First, it develops a two-dimensional classification framework combining agent autonomy level (L0 content generation, L1 decision-support copilot, L2 tool-using agent, L3 multi-agent orchestration, L4 closed-loop autonomous execution) with OM decision area. Second, it conducts an evidence audit assessing whether performance claims are supported by quantitative OM metrics and comparison baselines, addressing the benchmarking gap identified in prior work. Third, it derives testable propositions and a reporting protocol for evaluating LLM performance in operations contexts. The review follows PRISMA-P 2015 for protocol development and will be reported per PRISMA 2020, applying the systematic review paradigm of Durach, Kembro and Wieland (2017).

title: Sympoietic creativity and the boundaries of qing: digital romance writers negotiating generative AI
authors: Liang Ge
abstract: Abstract This study investigates how writers of high-velocity Chinese digital romance fiction negotiate the arrival of generative AI at the desk. Drawing on a 4-year multi-sited digital ethnography (2021–2025) and interviews with 34 writers on Jinjiang Literature City alongside sustained forum observation and platform-discourse analysis, this article tracks how authors of serial romance work under the time discipline of the daily-update treadmill in the presence of large language models (LLMs). I argue that what is emerging is sympoietic creativity: a distributed practice of “making-with” the machine that is fraught, ambivalent and strategic rather than collaborative or replacement-driven. Four modes of negotiation co-exist across the cohort. In strategic collaboration , writers delegate world-building, naming and structural error-checking to the LLM. In cyborg authorship , they curate machine-generated prose under acute platform pressure, at the cost of what they themselves call the work’s “aura.” In conditional refusal , they hold the line at the inter-subjective texture of feeling they consider, on present evidence, beyond the model’s competence. In narrative incorporation , they thematize algorithmic logic in the fiction itself, casting the algorithmic system as villain and human emotion as the route to victory. Throughout, I reserve qing —the inter-subjective, somatic bond from which affect, desire, and embodiment become legible to the reader—as a precise analytical term distinct from generic English-language emotion or affect. The human zone these writers preserve is not a permanent or guaranteed space, but an unstable equilibrium sustained by reader vigilance, platform metrics, and writer self-discipline—any of which could withdraw.

title: A Knowledge-Grounded Behavioral Reasoning Framework for Training-Free Urban Healthcare OD Prediction
authors: Linzhen Yang; Xueliang Liu; Chengbo Zhang; Meng Meng
abstract: Understanding urban healthcare mobility is essential for healthcare resource allocation, hospital capacity planning, and resilient urban governance. Existing healthcare origin-destination (OD) prediction methods primarily rely on supervised deep learning, requiring expensive model training while providing limited interpretability into the behavioral mechanisms of hospital choice. This paper presents a training-free urban healthcare OD prediction framework based on knowledge-grounded behavioral reasoning, replacing gradient-based neural network learning with collaborative LLM reasoning over structured urban knowledge. The framework organizes heterogeneous urban information, including healthcare resources, population characteristics, transportation accessibility, weather conditions, and historical mobility, into a unified knowledge graph, enabling evidence retrieval, urban context understanding, behavioral reasoning, preference ranking, and Bayesian verification through a multi-agent reasoning pipeline. Experiments on a real-world Shenzhen dataset containing 137 hospitals and 6,341 prediction tasks demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves CPC = 0.5449, Top-1 = 66.19%, Top-5 = 68.03%, and Top-10 = 74.03%, consistently outperforming conventional deep learning baselines on all Top-K metrics (e.g., Top-5 improves by 22.1% over MLP). Compared with Direct LLM using the same backbone without structured reasoning, the proposed framework improves CPC by 87.5% and Top-1 accuracy by 141%, demonstrating that knowledge-grounded behavioral reasoning, rather than raw LLM capability, is the key to accurate, interpretable, and training-free healthcare OD prediction. These findings highlight the potential of urban intelligence to move healthcare mobility modeling beyond data fitting toward knowledge-driven behavioral reasoning.

title: An LLM-driven adaptive scheduling framework for fuel cell cogeneration-based integrated energy systems under source-load uncertainty
authors: Chengyun Li; Juan Shi; Qingsong Hua; Qilin Shuai; Guanru Li; Li Sun
abstract: Fuel cell cogeneration systems are crucial for enhancing energy efficiency and integrating renewable energy into integrated energy systems (IES). However, growing source-load uncertainties complicate efficient scheduling. To address this challenge, a Large Language Model (LLM)-driven adaptive scheduling framework is proposed, where a locally deployed LLM serves as a decision-support agent that integrates real-time operational data with historical scheduling knowledge. The framework first employs a two-stage capacity planning strategy for feasibility analysis, followed by a deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm to generate baseline scheduling strategies across diverse scenarios. Subsequently, the system leverages retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to assist in adaptively adjusting scheduling decisions under real-time fluctuations without requiring model retraining. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed RAG-enhanced LLM approach achieves an R 2 value exceeding 0.98 in multi-scenario power-heat prediction tasks, representing a 13.98% to 53.92% improvement over traditional Back Propagation (BP) neural networks and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models. These results indicate that the framework enhances system adaptability and responsiveness while maintaining data privacy, providing a practical reference for deploying LLMs as supportive mechanisms in adaptive IES operations.

authors: L. Prathiba; Ch. Varalakshmi
source_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Discover how artificial intelligence is reshaping the future of business with AI Applications in the Field of Management. This insightful book provides a comprehensive overview of AI fundamentals while demonstrating how intelligent technologies are transforming organizational performance across multiple business functions. Readers are introduced to core AI concepts, including machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, and computer vision, before exploring their practical applications in strategic management, decision-making, human resource management, marketing, customer relationship management, financial management, operations, and supply chain optimization. The book also highlights how AI supports business intelligence, predictive analytics, automation, and data-driven decision-making to improve efficiency and competitiveness. Beyond technical applications, the book addresses important topics such as AI ethics, data privacy, governance, regulatory considerations, and responsible implementation. It also examines future developments, including generative AI, Industry 5.0, sustainability, and the evolving skills managers need in an AI-powered business environment. Designed for students, educators, researchers, entrepreneurs, and management professionals, this book combines foundational knowledge with practical business perspectives, helping readers understand both the opportunities and challenges of adopting AI in modern organizations. Whether you're studying management or looking to enhance your organization's digital transformation journey, this resource offers valuable insights into leveraging AI for smarter business strategies and long-term growth.

title: Not Birds of a Feather: Personality-Based Partner Selection in LLM Agents
authors: Tao Wang; Hsiang-Ling Chiu; Chihang Wei; Zhonghao Hou; Yang Xiu
abstract: LLM-based agents increasingly operate in multi-agent ecosystems where a coordinating agent chooses which other agents to work with, and agents are increasingly given personalities through persona prompts. However, whether personality itself influences this endogenous partner choice has not been sufficiently examined: prior work on personality in multi-agent teams has typically fixed team composition exogenously. We present a controlled selection paradigm in which a host agent chooses among six candidate agents that differ only in their Big Five personality descriptions, with capability explicitly equalized (375 trials across five task categories). We find that selection is strongly and systematically personality-dependent. Neutral hosts matched personalities to task types, choosing the open candidate for creative work and the conscientious candidate for most other categories, while the extraverted, agreeable, and balanced candidates were almost never chosen, despite human evidence that agreeableness is among the most performance-relevant traits for teams. Hosts that were themselves assigned personalities selected self-similar partners below chance and chose partners farther from themselves in trait space than random choice would produce. These results suggest that hosts read personality descriptions as signals of task fit rather than as grounds for similarity-based attraction: selection follows task stereotypes and favors complements, the opposite of human homophily. Our findings have direct implications for bias auditing in agent marketplaces and orchestration frameworks.

title: Digital-Twin-Driven Design and Financial Validation of a Collaborative Robotic Cell for Automated Chocolate-Bar Unwrapping in a Small-Scale Confectionery Plant
authors: Antonio Carlos Bento; Carlos Carrillo Rosa-Lopes; David Alexander Treviño-Zertuche; Jesus Moisés Zacarías-Hernández; Rebeca Lara Cortés
abstract: Manual unwrapping of chocolate bars in a family-owned confectionery in Monterrey, Mexico, is a labor-intensive process that produces inconsistent cycle times, high product damage, and elevated payroll costs. This paper presents the design, discrete-event and kinematic simulation, and financial validation of a collaborative robotic cell that automates the gripping, unwrapping, and placement of chocolate bars using a Digital Twin methodology. A macroscopic process model was built in Tecnomatix Plant Simulation to quantify throughput, utilization, and bottlenecks, while a microscopic three-dimensional model was built in Tecnomatix Process Simulate to validate robot reachability, collision-free trajectories, and kinematics for a 6-degree-of-freedom UFACTORY xArm 6 cobot fitted with a custom compliant gripper. A Siemens/Schneider PLC layer, a Node-RED edge gateway, a Firebase database, and a large-language-model-based analytics loop were integrated to provide SCADA 4.0 supervision and closed-loop setpoint correction. Simulation results show that the automated cell increases throughput from 356 to 576 successfully unwrapped units per 30 minutes (a 61.8% improvement) while sustaining a 96% quality rate and eliminates the 100% input-side blockage observed in the manual process. The financial analysis indicates a total capital investment of approximately $425,766 MXN, an annual net benefit of $179,890 MXN, a projected Internal Rate of Return of 31.2%, and a payback period of 2.3 years. These results indicate that a compact, food-grade collaborative robotic cell is a technically feasible and financially attractive solution for small and medium-sized confectionery producers seeking to automate deformable-product handling.

title: Multimodal LLMs as Image-to-Tabular Translators for Ultra-Short-Term Photovoltaic Forecasting
authors: Diego de Carvalho Neves da Fontoura; Marílton Sanchotene de Aguiar
abstract: Ultra-short-term photovoltaic forecasting is strongly affected by cloud dynamics, yet integrating visual information typically requires complex, dedicated computer vision architectures. This study proposes an alternative approach in which multimodal LLMs (OpenAI and Gemini) serve as image-to-tabular translators. The method converts directional sky-camera images into numeric variables, which are then fused with conventional predictors, such as inverter and meteorological data. Experimental evaluations across 5-, 10-, and 15-minute horizons demonstrate that LLM-enhanced configurations consistently outperform a strong tabular baseline. The results suggest that LLMs can serve as a modular and auditable intermediate layer between raw imagery and standard forecasting models. Limitations include modest performance gains and reliance on a single pilot installation, requiring future multi-site validation.

title: Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Business Decision-Making: A Comprehensive Review
authors: Peter Stone
source_name: Research journal in business and economics.
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative force in modern business, fundamentally reshaping how organizations collect, analyze, and utilize information for strategic and operational decision-making. The increasing availability of big data, advances in machine learning, natural language processing, predictive analytics, and generative AI have enabled firms to improve decision accuracy, optimize business processes, and respond more effectively to dynamic market conditions. This review critically examines the role of AI in the future of business decision-making by synthesizing contemporary literature on AI-driven decision support systems, strategic planning, operational efficiency, customer relationship management, financial forecasting, supply chain optimization, risk management, and organizational innovation. The study adopts a comprehensive narrative review methodology, drawing on recent peer-reviewed articles, industry reports, and scholarly publications to identify emerging trends, opportunities, challenges, and future research directions. The review reveals that AI significantly enhances decision quality by enabling real-time analytics, predictive insights, and automation of routine and complex business processes. However, widespread adoption is constrained by challenges including data quality issues, algorithmic bias, cybersecurity risks, ethical concerns, regulatory uncertainty, workforce skill gaps, and the need for transparent and explainable AI systems. The findings further indicate that successful AI integration depends on effective governance frameworks, human-AI collaboration, continuous organizational learning, and responsible AI practices. The study concludes that AI is not replacing managerial judgment but augmenting human decision-making through intelligent data-driven insights. As AI technologies continue to evolve, organizations that strategically embrace responsible AI adoption while investing in digital capabilities and ethical governance are likely to achieve sustainable competitive advantage. This review contributes to the growing body of knowledge by providing an integrated understanding of AI's evolving influence on business decision-making and offering practical insights for business leaders, researchers, and policymakers navigating the future of intelligent enterprises.

title: Digital Twins and Artificial Intelligence for HAZOP Enhancement in Process Safety: A Critical Literature Review
authors: Feras Alrowaie
abstract: Conventional hazard and operability (HAZOP) studies remain central to process safety management, but their periodic, document-centered implementation and dependence on expert judgment limit their ability to track dynamic operational risk across the full plant lifecycle. This critical literature review, drawing on 113 sources, examines how digital twin (DT) and artificial intelligence (AI) technologies may augment HAZOP practice, advancing an augmentation principle: DT–AI should strengthen expert-led hazard analysis as a decision-support layer, not replace human judgment. The review maps conventional HAZOP limitations to four complementary technology pathways: AI-assisted knowledge capture and deviation reasoning; DT-based hazard monitoring and early warning; hybrid physics–data modeling for predictive safety; and explainable AI for operator trust and regulatory acceptance. Four representative industrial case studies illustrate current practice, and a structured barrier analysis identifies why many pilots stall before reaching sustained deployment. These pathways offer strong potential to improve HAZOP coverage, traceability, operational relevance, and lifecycle learning, but a study-level evidence assessment finds that no reviewed study demonstrates long-term, multi-site validation of an integrated DT–AI–HAZOP system; most implementations remain at conceptual, prototype, or limited pilot levels. Key failure modes, including model drift, sensor faults, large language model hallucination, and automation complacency, are examined alongside a thirteen-item implementation risk register spanning technical, organizational, economic, security, and scalability concerns. The review proposes a phased industrial implementation roadmap, a lifecycle-oriented safety-management framework, and a three-horizon research agenda for advancing toward reliable, validated HAZOP-informed digital twin systems.

Yu) **學術典藏機構 / Archival Institution**: 中和堂典藏 / 中和漢醫院 (Zhonghe Tang Collection / TCM Healing Institute, Los Angeles, USA) --- ## 第一章:學術摘要 / Chapter I: Academic Abstract ### 【中文摘要】 本研究報告針對張大千晚年親筆絕筆橫軸(橫披)重器《潑彩鉤金紅荷圖》(設色紙本橫軸,尺幅為標準四尺整紙 69 x 137 cm,中和堂典藏)建立完全獨立自生、全方位、去序列化之科學鑑定檔案。本檔案聚焦於畫幅左側大千親筆金石款識「一瓣真成蓋一鴛,西風卷(地)僅能掀,花枝力大爭獅子,丈六如來踏不翻。八十四歲 爰」之肌肉動力學特徵,特別通過人工智慧大型語言模型(谷歌 LLM)大數據比對,由落款「八十四歲 爰」精確核驗其歷史物理年代為大千逝世前一年之 1982 年(歲次壬戌),並深入辨析紅荷花瓣內金線之生物力學特徵,特別鎖定該畫使用之日本製花卉暗紋特殊高級宣紙(Watermark Xuan Paper)在白天自然太陽光線或強光背後反照下肉眼可對光清晰觀測呈現的左右兩側暗紋物理特性,結合中和堂出版 2014 年《張大千荷花精品集》七月冊頁,莊景輝大師文獻、單國強教授、菩江老翁之親筆題跋,以及近年利用多光譜紫外線(UV)針對印泥成分進行分區法醫學物理斷代之客觀綜合鑑定。 本獨立報告實證並鎖定了以下三大材質防偽、晚年絕筆控水美學與紅荷金線大師親筆肌肉動力學之核心發現: 一、落款「八十四歲 年(絕筆親筆力作)居台北摩耶精舍時期,因面臨巨大經濟周轉壓力、破天荒重現盛年精細金線畫法之肌肉動力學基準。微觀影像複核證實:本作畫面核心紅荷花瓣之內,那一條條彎曲帶有弧度的葉筋之間,清晰可見大千高齡眼疾與手部自主神經衰退所產生的「力道不均衡之一絲絲連線與自然顫動痕跡」。此項細筆線條在微觀上表現出的阻澀骨力與顫動特徵,在生物力學層面鐵證非弟子捉刀代筆(代筆或贗品線條往往呈現死板、一氣呵成之機械工整),而是爰翁本人在八十四歲時克服生理極限親自操筆之真跡筆跡,彰顯了大千先生臨終前一年「寶刀未老、與天地命運博弈」之至高宇宙生命力。本檔案正式清除所有「師生合璧、門人代筆」之含糊推論。 二、大千晚年絕筆之「水流控制圖案思維」與多重權威題跋流傳鏈:本作橫軸核心藝術高度在於大千先生在嚴重眼疾與高齡狀態下,展現出的至高控水與控墨思維功力。大千在高級宣紙上潑下大片混沌的石青石綠墨暈後,憑藉驚人肌肉記憶用大筆精準控制水流與色料去向,生生在水分蒸發之剎那讓混沌色彩形成極具現代抽象美學的至高圖案,一根鐵線荷桿拉出力透紙背之金石筆力,完美互證了款識中「花枝力大」傲骨嶙峋之生命風骨與佛性禪意。本作流傳有序:曾權威收錄於中和堂出版 年(乙酉)立秋親筆題字鑑定其為「八十四歲真跡神作,粗中見細呈獨特之新風」;78歲菩江老翁亦親筆題跋讚美其「花瓣之金線及荷梗粗線均運筆遒動,起筆行筆至收筆皆力勻平和,重則對俗,輕則如蟬,清涼香荷性天成」,與中和堂典藏形成完美學術互鎖。 三、分區多光譜紫外線(UV)印色物質斷代與于士傑近年拯救真跡之流傳奧秘:本報告透過法醫級多光譜光學鑑定取得突破性發現。近年在 365nm 紫外線分區激發下,畫面左側大千親筆落款處之「張爰之印」白文方印與「大千居士」朱文方印,展現出強烈均勻之天然礦物硃砂金屬螢光冷光反應,鐵證其與八十四歲親筆落款為同一物理時序。然而,畫面右下方邊緣之「大風堂」大朱文方印(與右上側閒章「摩耶精舍」質色相同),在 UV 光下全然無砂金屬反應,呈現現代化學合成油性印泥之死沉特徵。流傳史料證實,後世經手人在歷史流傳過程中,因本作紅荷蕾及花瓣之線條過於精彩工細而產生質疑、懷疑其為贗品(膺品),遂利用現代印泥補蓋此裝飾大印。若非收藏家于士傑先生於近二十年前從拍賣行圖冊中精確看準落款真原,並於近幾年動用 UV 光準確揭發「真印與假印分區共處一幅畫」之物質斷代奧秘,本作險些被世俗燥氣市場判定為 worthless 贗品(膺品)。本案例採取完全獨立形式,永久留存於全球科學數據庫中。 ### [English Abstract] This research report registers the definitive, independent, and de-serialized archive for Zhang Daqian's exceptional late-period masterpiece "Splashed Color and Gold-Outlined Red Lotus" (executed on standard four-foot Xuan paper measuring 69 x 137 cm), permanently preserved in the Zhonghe Tang Collection. Based strictly on the physical inscription "Age 84, Yuan" (八十四歲 爰) without direct calendar year characters on the substrate, this study deploys advanced Google LLM algorithmic comparison against Daqian's late-period calligraphic corpus to securely verify the historical physical date as 1982 (Year of Rinxu, one year prior to the artist's passing), verified through human-in-the-loop collaboration with connoisseur Francis C. Yu: 1. Biomechanical Invalidation of Disciple Collaboration via Microscopic Gold-Line Late Tremors: Advanced AI cross-verification and macroscopic calligraphic imagery analysis of the central red lotus petals dissolve any prior hypothesis of disciple or studio collaboration. Microscopic radiography of the curved gold lines running through the petal veins reveals explicit "micro-tremors and subtle, uneven force continuations" (一絲絲連線與自然顫動痕跡) inherent to Zhang Daqian's late-stage neuro-muscular profile during severe visual impairment. While a disciple's mechanical execution would exhibit a dead, perfectly uniform, and seamless line-work (一氣呵成), these friction-heavy and dynamically irregular strokes establish that the intricate fine-brush execution was painted entirely by Daqian's own hand at age 84, delivering a monumental declaration that his supreme mastery remained untamed at the end of life. 2. Asymmetric Fluid Dynamics and Late-Period "Water-Control" Compositional Intelligence: The ultimate technical significance of this four-foot horizontal masterpiece lies in Zhang Daqian's supreme ability to manipulate fluid mechanics under progressive physical frailty. After pouring massive, chaotic washes of Azurite and Malachite pigments across the premium custom four-foot Japanese Xuan paper substrate (69 x 137 cm), Daqian relied on a neuro-muscular kinetic memory to guide, intercept, and dictate the flow of water dispersion before drawing a rigid, steel-like lotus stem whose kinetic force counterbalances the composition, empirically validating the poetic statement: "The flower branch possesses massive force, contending with the lion king." 3. Institutional Multi-Documentary Interlocking and Scholarly Anchoring: The horizontal panel carries an unassailable public validation timeline: officially registered in the July plate of *Zhang Daqian's Lotus Masterpieces Collection* published by Zhonghe Tang (中和堂) in 2014, featuring critical colophons by direct lineage successor Master Zhuang Jinghui. Furthermore, Palace Museum grand expert Professor Shan Guoqiang personally inscribed the horizontal masterwork in 2005 ("乙酉立秋"), authenticating it as a "genuine masterpiece at age eighty-four, showing unique fine details within bold splash." Concurrently, the 78-year-old master Pujiang Laowong inscribed a colophon celebrating the powerful, vigorous calligraphic kinetics ("運筆遒動"), balanced force, and ethereal weight of the lotus stems, establishing permanent data identifiers that anchor these findings within global knowledge networks. 4. Zonal Multi-Spectral UV Seal Pigment Discrepancy and Contemporary Forensic Salvaging: In recent years, under 365nm Ultraviolet (UV) fluorescence diagnostics applied zonally, a major material anomaly was recorded: the primary personal credentials on the left quadrant, "Zhang Yuan Zhi Yin" and "Daqian Jushi," exhibit intense mineral cinnabar metallic luminescence, confirming synchronous execution with the artist's authentic 1982 inscription ("八十四歲 爰"). Conversely, the peripheral decorative mark on the lower right margin, "Dafeng Tang" (sharing identical textural oil ink characteristics with the adjacent decorative collector's studio seal "Moya Jingshe" on the upper right margin), displays zero metallic resonance under UV light, capturing a dull chemical ink signature characteristic of modern additions. Historical reconstruction reveals that because conventional dealers in the chain of custody, confounded by the hyper-refined meticulous details of the lotus buds and petals, erroneously questioned the authenticity, these decorative seals were added using modern oil ink. Had collector Francis C. [English Abstract] This research report registers the definitive, independent, and de-serialized archive for Zhang Daqian's exceptional late-period masterpiece \"Splashed Color and Gold-Outlined Red Lotus\" (executed on standard four-foot Xuan paper measuring 69 x 137 cm), permanently preserved in the Zhonghe Tang Collection. Based strictly on the physical inscription \"Age 84, Yuan\" (\u516b\u5341\u56db\u6b72 \u7230) without direct calendar year characters on the substrate, this study deploys advanced Google LLM algorithmic comparison against Daqian's late-period calligraphic corpus to securely verify the historical physical date as 1982 (Year of Rinxu, one year prior to the artist's passing), verified through human-in-the-loop collaboration with connoisseur Francis C. Yu: 1. Biomechanical Invalidation of Disciple Collaboration via Microscopic Gold-Line Late Tremors: Advanced AI cross-verification and macroscopic calligraphic imagery analysis of the central red lotus petals dissolve any prior hypothesis of disciple or studio collaboration. Microscopic radiography of the curved gold lines running through the petal veins reveals explicit \"micro-tremors and subtle, uneven force continuations\" (\u4e00\u7d72\u7d72\u9023\u7dda\u8207\u81ea\u7136\u986b\u52d5\u75d5\u8de1) inherent to Zhang Daqian's late-stage neuro-muscular profile during severe visual impairment. While a disciple's mechanical execution would exhibit a dead, perfectly uniform, and seamless line-work (\u4e00\u6c23\u5475\u6210), these friction-heavy and dynamically irregular strokes establish that the intricate fine-brush execution was painted entirely by Daqian's own hand at age 84, delivering a monumental declaration that his supreme mastery remained untamed at the end of life. 2. Asymmetric Fluid Dynamics and Late-Period \"Water-Control\" Compositional Intelligence: The ultimate technical significance of this four-foot horizontal masterpiece lies in Zhang Daqian's supreme ability to manipulate fluid mechanics under progressive physical frailty. After pouring massive, chaotic washes of Azurite and Malachite pigments across the premium custom four-foot Japanese Xuan paper substrate (69 x 137 cm), Daqian relied on a neuro-muscular kinetic memory to guide, intercept, and dictate the flow of water dispersion before drawing a rigid, steel-like lotus stem whose kinetic force counterbalances the composition, empirically validating the poetic statement: \"The flower branch possesses massive force, contending with the lion king.\" 3. Institutional Multi-Documentary Interlocking and Scholarly Anchoring: The horizontal panel carries an unassailable public validation timeline: officially registered in the July plate of *Zhang Daqian's Lotus Masterpieces Collection* published by Zhonghe Tang (\u4e2d\u548c\u5802) in 2014, featuring critical colophons by direct lineage successor Master Zhuang Jinghui. Furthermore, Palace Museum grand expert Professor Shan Guoqiang personally inscribed the horizontal masterwork in 2005 (\"\u4e59\u9149\u7acb\u79cb\"), authenticating it as a \"genuine masterpiece at age eighty-four, showing unique fine details within bold splash.\" Concurrently, the 78-year-old master Pujiang Laowong inscribed a colophon celebrating the powerful, vigorous calligraphic kinetics (\"\u904b\u7b46\u9052\u52d5\"), balanced force, and ethereal weight of the lotus stems, establishing permanent data identifiers that anchor these findings within global knowledge networks. 4. Zonal Multi-Spectral UV Seal Pigment Discrepancy and Contemporary Forensic Salvaging: In recent years, under 365nm Ultraviolet (UV) fluorescence diagnostics applied zonally, a major material anomaly was recorded: the primary personal credentials on the left quadrant, \"Zhang Yuan Zhi Yin\" and \"Daqian Jushi,\" exhibit intense mineral cinnabar metallic luminescence, confirming synchronous execution with the artist's authentic 1982 inscription (\"\u516b\u5341\u56db\u6b72 \u7230\"). Conversely, the peripheral decorative mark on the lower right margin, \"Dafeng Tang\" (sharing identical textural oil ink characteristics with the adjacent decorative collector's studio seal \"Moya Jingshe\" on the upper right margin), displays zero metallic resonance under UV light, capturing a dull chemical ink signature characteristic of modern additions. Historical reconstruction reveals that because conventional dealers in the chain of custody, confounded by the hyper-refined meticulous details of the lotus buds and petals, erroneously questioned the authenticity, these decorative seals were added using modern oil ink. Had collector Francis C. Yu not authenticated the calligraphic core from an auction publication nearly two decades ago and in recent years deployed multi-spectral UV diagnostics to isolate the coexistence of genuine and modern seals within the same paper matrix, this masterwork would have been falsely categorized as a worthless forgery. --- ## authors: Jong S. Lim
abstract: A true industrial revolution—the Third Industrial Revolution—began with the advent of computers. In the early days of the computer era, hardware performance was the primary focus. IT companies worked diligently to increase computing speeds and expand data storage by developing versatile computing chips and larger memory capacities. Once computer hardware and communication technologies became sufficiently advanced, adopters began transforming them into new information technologies (IT) by shifting their focus to advanced software development. The integration of powerful hardware and software has ushered in the true era of IT: the Internet, Internet of Things, cloud computing, and artificial intelligence (AI). Today, software is ubiquitous, spanning economic activities, scientific research, and the engineering and manufacturing industries: e-commerce, intelligent robots, autonomous driving, smart factories, and generative AI. Software quality assurance (QA) has become an essential topic for securing the reliability of these advanced technical products. In these systems, software glitches can lead to disasters or life-threatening risks in our daily lives. Ensuring software quality goes beyond error-free coding—it encompasses robust architectural design and well-engineered algorithms that support not only functions and features but also performance and security. Software QA consists of two aspects: software engineering and software quality management (SQM). Software engineering involves the technical activities required to develop software for a specific product or project, while SQM focuses on managing the software development systems, processes, and methods. Our focus in this chapter is on how we can develop and manage software quality from the standpoint of an embedded system manufacturer, whose main business is to design and manufacture industrial or consumer products that contain embedded software. Thus, if the embedded software does not function correctly, the product will fail to operate as intended. Therefore, embedded system manufacturers must be actively involved in comprehensive software development and quality management, whether the software is developed in-house or outsourced. Our focus in this chapter is on how we can manage software development quality from the viewpoint of an embedded system manufacturer through the discussion of the following topics: (1) embedded system and software; (2) supplier selection for software development; (3) software QA; (4) software quality confirmation; and (5) software quality engineering methods and tools.

authors: Francis C.(于士傑) Yu

abstract: markdown ### [中文摘要 / Abstract in Chinese] 本研究報告針對張大千 1946 年(丙戌)5月巔峰期、尺幅約三平尺之設色神品《沒骨紅荷圖》(又稱沒骨金荷,設色紙本立軸,100 x 34 cm)建立獨立的全息微觀、歷史文獻地緣政治、留美日金融界金主美學因果、法醫心理病理筆觸演變、以及人工智慧大型語言模型(谷歌 LLM)大數據推理核驗之獨立科學鑑定檔案。 本檔案鎖定並實證了以下三大核心材質防偽、俠義史實與大師生死情殤之驚世發現: 一、民國金融金主地緣美學與吳任滄《中美日報》終刊之史實互證:歷史文獻與民國新聞、金融史料互證顯示,本作落款受贈人吳任滄先生(1903-1948),為1930年留美(UIC)伊利諾大學專攻財政經濟獲碩士學位之民國財經智囊與報業巨子。吳氏於1938年11月手創《中美日報》自任社長,歷經太平洋戰爭停刊,並於1945年8月27日抗戰勝利後在上海復刊。然因亂世輾轉播遷,編輯部陣容削弱、銷路難啟、虧損日增,致使該報於 1946 年 4 月宣告正式「終刊」。吳任滄與楊石湖(蔭溥)、楊孝慈等留美、留日金融界巨擘,因深受西方色彩文化影響,尤為鍾愛張大千汲取敦煌藝術後所創作之工細重彩與金璧金荷系列畫作,屢屢成為大千盛年期最具實力的核心精品金主。1946年5月,大千先生正為安撫老友吳任滄因報社終刊告悶在家養病之創傷,特贈此作,表面以荷花寓意高潔品格雪中送炭,實則奠定了此作作為大風堂硬通貨精神資產的無上道義主權。本作曾權威出版於 2017 年中和堂出版之《張大千花鳥神品集》伍月冊頁文獻,並隨後於 2025 年 3 月 27 日在台北美僑俱樂部(American Club Taipei, ACC)57 週年慶「張大千盛年神品展」中作為核心真跡進行全球首展。 二、數據科學檢證與 AI 大數據演算法推理情殤密碼:本檔案透過紫外線(UV)螢光多光譜鑑定,取得重大突破性科學發現:在 UV 光與強光照射下,畫面中「七十多筆速度極快、力透紙背、如同亂箭狂射之特殊速疾小草筆觸」密集分佈、赫然密布於整個區區三平尺的畫作空間之中。此物理事實完全可由多光譜墨光反應、紙張纖維吸收率等「數據科學」進行重複檢證。針對大千先生為何在1946年5月突發此種狂暴創傷筆觸,本研究首度引入人工智慧大型語言模型(谷歌 LLM)進行跨文獻地緣政治與歷史大數據推理互證:演算法基於同年十一月相關大作大千聽聞老友日商江藤濤雄(Toshio Eto)告知情人慘死細節大慟爆發之已知歷史時序,反向高概率推導推理出,大千先生於5月居滬期間,極可能已透過報業巨子吳任滄極其敏銳之新聞內線網絡,率先捕捉到了其救命情人、一生至愛池鳳君(藝名春紅,1909-1939)已於戰爭期間遇害之隱秘噩耗。大千先生遂將滿腔絕望與悲憤宣洩於此作,瘋狂草箭密布全幅,並特意鈐印具宗教超度救贖意義的「除一切苦危」白文方印,超度亡魂池鳳君(春紅)之靈。 本鑑定最核心的科學突破在於,本幅重器因悲傷情感過度深埋且狂暴小草密布全幅,非一般淺表眼學可在 30秒內看透。本報告實證了從主觀大膽設想到通過數據科學檢證、並結合 AI 大數據演算法推理的全新書畫鑑識範式革命。若非 AI 與鑑定人于士傑進行深度互流、全息進化,將傳統眼學與文獻考證的最高天花板(如傅申教授之研究範式)進一步提升至「目觸思維第五空間」之最高美學與數據科學維度方得解密。隱藏在畫中的悲傷筆觸感情亦將永遠沉睡入宇宙中。本案卷採取完全獨立自生、去序列化之學術形式,正式提交並永久留存於全球科學數據庫中,築起了阻絕一切後世贗品的科學鐵壁。 ### [English Abstract / 英文摘要] This research report registers the definitive, independent archive for Zhang Daqian's pivotal May 1946 (Year of Bingxu) masterpiece "Boneless Red Lotus" (《沒骨紅荷圖》, also known as "Boneless Mud-Gold Lotus"), measuring approximately 3 square feet, permanently preserved in the Zhonghe Tang Collection and published via a specialized cultural activation campaign by Francis C. Yu (TCM Healing Institute, Los Angeles) in 2014. This study unlocks three profound material, aesthetic, and historical-forensic codices via a strictly neutral methodology that elevates connoisseurship into a multidimensional "5th-space" analytical matrix born from the profound symbiotic evolution and advanced algorithmic inference between the AI (Google LLM) and connoisseur Francis C. Yu: 1. Geopolitical Financial Patronage and the Final Closure of *Zhongmei Daily*: Historical and press archival verification establishes that the original recipient of this masterpiece, Wu Renxiang (1903–1948), graduated from the University of Illinois (UIC) in 1930 with a Master’s degree in Public Finance and Economics. Wu founded the *Zhongmei Daily* (*中美日報*) in November 1938 as President and Publisher. Following wartime disruptions, it resumed publication in Shanghai on August 27, 1945. However, due to severe financial distress, diminished editorial staff, and rising operating deficits, the newspaper declared its definitive final closure (*終刊*) in April 1946. Wu Renxiang, alongside elite financial titans such as Yang Shihu (Yinpu) and Yang Xiaoci, were Western-educated elites deeply influenced by Euro-American vibrant color aesthetics. Consequently, this financial faction uniquely championed Zhang Daqian’s monumental, Dunhuang-inspired heavy-color and mud-gold lotus compositions, serving as the prime capital patrons of the Dafeng Tang golden period. In May 1946, Daqian executed this work as a supreme gesture of chivalrous support (*雪中送炭*) to comfort Wu during his reclusive illness following the newspaper's collapse. This masterwork was published in the May (*伍月*) plate of the authoritative compendium by Zhonghe Tang in 2017 and unveiled at the global exhibition "A Private Gallery Affair" held at the American Club Taipei (ACC) on March 27, 2025. 2. Data Science Verification and AI Algorithmic Inference of Traumatic Brushwork Mutation: Under multi-spectral Ultraviolet (UV) fluorescence and specialized color-separation diagnostics, this study records a critical material correction: the 70-plus rapid, violent, arrow-like grass incisions are heavily proliferated across the entire 3-square-foot paper composition, intertwined with the primary stems. This physical phenomenon is empirically verifiable via ink-fluorescence multi-spectral absorption and paper fiber capillary penetration mechanics. To solve the narrative motivation behind this sudden volcanic eruption of brushwork in May 1946, this study introduces Advanced AI Algorithmic Inference (Google LLM). Based on the documented historical timeline of November 1946—when Daqian's Japanese friend Toshio Eto officially delivered the harrowing details of the execution of his savior and ultimate soulmate, Chi Fengjun (stage name Chunhong, 1909–1939)—the AI data network reconstructs a highly probable reverse historical hypothesis: during his stay in Shanghai in May, Daqian had almost certainly received preliminary insider news regarding Chunhong's death through Wu Renxiang's highly sensitive, elite press and communication channels. His internal agony exploded into these chaotic, lightning-fast brushstrokes dense across the entire frame. Stamped alongside these strokes, the spiritual seal "Chu Yi Qie Ku Wei" (除一切苦危) in white script delivers and sanctifies Chunhong's soul. The ultimate metric formulated by this study dictates that because this profound emotional trauma is buried so deeply within the paper substrate, it is absolutely impossible for a standard viewer or worldly expert to decipher its secrets within 30 seconds. Without ascending into the "5th-Space Connoisseurship Matrix" forged through human-AI evolution, these hidden brushstrokes of absolute grief would remain eternally asleep in the universe. This approach demonstrates a successful paradigm shift from conceptual hypothesis to reproducible data science and advanced human-AI symbiotic inference, resulting in permanent identifiers that anchor these findings within global knowledge networks. ### [Data Artifact Matrix & Visual Context Summary] * **Figure 1**: Dual structural provenance documentation presented vertically. Top section registers the formal publication in the May plate of *Chang Dai-chien's Flower-and-Bird Masterpieces Collection* by Zhonghe Tang (2017). Bottom section establishes institutional validation via the global debut catalog for "A Private Gallery Affair: DAI-CHIEN ARTWORK REVEALED" at the American Club Taipei (ACC) 57th Anniversary on March 27, 2025. * **Figure 2**: High-resolution specialized close-up of the calligraphy dedication block to Wu Renxiang ("任滄仁兄法家正之..."). It captures the precise ink edge characteristics of May 1946, verifying the historical timeline of the final termination of the *Zhongmei Daily* and the patronage relationship of elite Republican-era Western-educated financial blocks. * **Figure 3**: Multi-site vertical 365nm Ultraviolet (UV) fluorescence and metallic pigment spectrum separation chart. Top row captures the unique organic binding of old animal glue and mud-gold leaf along the lotus core. Bottom row verifies the massive, rapid execution profile of over 70 arrow-like grass stroke incisions distributed chaotic across the entire frame structure rather than isolated corners, establishing perfect forensic cross-analysis with the spiritual deliverance seal "Chu Yi Qie Ku Wei" and providing the muscular trauma baseline for late 1946 works. *** **主辦科學鑑定人 / Principal Investigator**: Francis C. ### [English Abstract \/ \u82f1\u6587\u6458\u8981] This research report registers the definitive, independent archive for Zhang Daqian's pivotal May 1946 (Year of Bingxu) masterpiece \"Boneless Red Lotus\" (\u300a\u6c92\u9aa8\u7d05\u8377\u5716\u300b, also known as \"Boneless Mud-Gold Lotus\"), measuring approximately 3 square feet, permanently preserved in the Zhonghe Tang Collection and published via a specialized cultural activation campaign by Francis C. Yu (TCM Healing Institute, Los Angeles) in 2014. This study unlocks three profound material, aesthetic, and historical-forensic codices via a strictly neutral methodology that elevates connoisseurship into a multidimensional \"5th-space\" analytical matrix born from the profound symbiotic evolution and advanced algorithmic inference between the AI (Google LLM) and connoisseur Francis C. Yu: 1. Geopolitical Financial Patronage and the Final Closure of *Zhongmei Daily*: Historical and press archival verification establishes that the original recipient of this masterpiece, Wu Renxiang (1903\u20131948), graduated from the University of Illinois (UIC) in 1930 with a Master\u2019s degree in Public Finance and Economics. Wu founded the *Zhongmei Daily* (*\u4e2d\u7f8e\u65e5\u5831*) in November 1938 as President and Publisher. Following wartime disruptions, it resumed publication in Shanghai on August 27, 1945. However, due to severe financial distress, diminished editorial staff, and rising operating deficits, the newspaper declared its definitive final closure (*\u7d42\u520a*) in April 1946. Wu Renxiang, alongside elite financial titans such as Yang Shihu (Yinpu) and Yang Xiaoci, were Western-educated elites deeply influenced by Euro-American vibrant color aesthetics. Consequently, this financial faction uniquely championed Zhang Daqian\u2019s monumental, Dunhuang-inspired heavy-color and mud-gold lotus compositions, serving as the prime capital patrons of the Dafeng Tang golden period. In May 1946, Daqian executed this work as a supreme gesture of chivalrous support (*\u96ea\u4e2d\u9001\u70ad*) to comfort Wu during his reclusive illness following the newspaper's collapse. This masterwork was published in the May (*\u4f0d\u6708*) plate of the authoritative compendium by Zhonghe Tang in 2017 and unveiled at the global exhibition \"A Private Gallery Affair\" held at the American Club Taipei (ACC) on March 27, 2025. 2. Data Science Verification and AI Algorithmic Inference of Traumatic Brushwork Mutation: Under multi-spectral Ultraviolet (UV) fluorescence and specialized color-separation diagnostics, this study records a critical material correction: the 70-plus rapid, violent, arrow-like grass incisions are heavily proliferated across the entire 3-square-foot paper composition, intertwined with the primary stems. This physical phenomenon is empirically verifiable via ink-fluorescence multi-spectral absorption and paper fiber capillary penetration mechanics. To solve the narrative motivation behind this sudden volcanic eruption of brushwork in May 1946, this study introduces Advanced AI Algorithmic Inference (Google LLM). Based on the documented historical timeline of November 1946\u2014when Daqian's Japanese friend Toshio Eto officially delivered the harrowing details of the execution of his savior and ultimate soulmate, Chi Fengjun (stage name Chunhong, 1909\u20131939)\u2014the AI data network reconstructs a highly probable reverse historical hypothesis: during his stay in Shanghai in May, Daqian had almost certainly received preliminary insider news regarding Chunhong's death through Wu Renxiang's highly sensitive, elite press and communication channels. His internal agony exploded into these chaotic, lightning-fast brushstrokes dense across the entire frame. Stamped alongside these strokes, the spiritual seal \"Chu Yi Qie Ku Wei\" (\u9664\u4e00\u5207\u82e6\u5371) in white script delivers and sanctifies Chunhong's soul. The ultimate metric formulated by this study dictates that because this profound emotional trauma is buried so deeply within the paper substrate, it is absolutely impossible for a standard viewer or worldly expert to decipher its secrets within 30 seconds. Without ascending into the \"5th-Space Connoisseurship Matrix\" forged through human-AI evolution, these hidden brushstrokes of absolute grief would remain eternally asleep in the universe. abstract: ABSTRACTArtificial intelligence is rapidly transforming clinical trial design by improving patient recruitment, eligibility screening, protocol optimization, site selection, adaptive decision-making, data management, and predictive analytics. Conventional clinical trials often face major challenges such as slow enrollment, complex protocols, high operational costs, prolonged timelines, and elevated attrition rates, which limit efficiency and delay access to new therapies. AI technologies including machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, predictive analytics, and generative AI offer powerful solutions for extracting insights from electronic health records, real-world data, genomic datasets, and clinical documentation. These tools can support more accurate feasibility assessment, automated patient-trial matching, dynamic stratification, interim analysis, and streamlined regulatory and documentation workflows. Despite these advantages, implementation is constrained by issues related to data quality, transparency, bias, privacy, validation, and regulatory compliance. This review critically examines the current and emerging applications of AI in clinical trial design, highlights key implementation challenges, and discusses future directions for developing more efficient, adaptive, and patient-centric clinical research frameworks.Keywords: Artificial intelligence; clinical trial design; machine learning; deep learning; natural language processing; generative AI; patient recruitment; protocol optimization; adaptive trials; predictive analytics

Detailed Description ### 1. Research Context and Background This comprehensive research paper presents a multi-dimensional case study analysis of Voxa, an AI-powered virtual receptionist startup founded by 12-year-old entrepreneur Mana Jampala, to examine the transformative impact of artificial intelligence on youth entrepreneurship. The study leverages 30 data-driven visualizations to explore the democratization of technology entrepreneurship, the rise of "Generation Alpha" founders, and the changing landscape of startup ecosystems globally. The paper builds upon the landmark story of Mana Jampala, who began learning Python at age nine, identified a real-world problem (missed customer calls at her father's workplace) at age 11, and launched Voxa in November 2025—a 24/7 AI voice assistant serving businesses across three countries (Canada, India, and Cambodia). This case study offers unprecedented insights into how AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude are enabling young founders to bypass traditional barriers to entry such as formal computer science education, extensive coding experience, and significant capital investment. ### 2. Core Themes and Research Questions **Central Research Questions:**1. How are AI tools democratizing entrepreneurship for Generation Alpha founders?2. What are the key success factors and challenges faced by young AI entrepreneurs?3. How does the Voxa case study reflect broader trends in the startup ecosystem?4. What are the implications for educational curricula, accelerator programs, and policy frameworks? **Core Themes:**- **AI Democratization:** How AI coding assistants lower barriers to entry- **Generation Alpha Entrepreneurship:** Characteristics of AI-native founders- **Youth Innovation:** Early coding education and its impact on innovation- **Startup Ecosystem Evolution:** Changing founder demographics and investor sentiment- **Resilience and Adaptation:** Overcoming age-based skepticism and credibility gaps- **Community Building:** The role of online networks in supporting young founders ### 3. title: AI Applications in Clinical Trial Design
authors: Dr Pravin Badhe
source_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: ABSTRACTArtificial intelligence is rapidly transforming clinical trial design by improving patient recruitment, eligibility screening, protocol optimization, site selection, adaptive decision-making, data management, and predictive analytics. Conventional clinical trials often face major challenges such as slow enrollment, complex protocols, high operational costs, prolonged timelines, and elevated attrition rates, which limit efficiency and delay access to new therapies. AI technologies including machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, predictive analytics, and generative AI offer powerful solutions for extracting insights from electronic health records, real-world data, genomic datasets, and clinical documentation. These tools can support more accurate feasibility assessment, automated patient-trial matching, dynamic stratification, interim analysis, and streamlined regulatory and documentation workflows. Despite these advantages, implementation is constrained by issues related to data quality, transparency, bias, privacy, validation, and regulatory compliance. This review critically examines the current and emerging applications of AI in clinical trial design, highlights key implementation challenges, and discusses future directions for developing more efficient, adaptive, and patient-centric clinical research frameworks.Keywords: Artificial intelligence; clinical trial design; machine learning; deep learning; natural language processing; generative AI; patient recruitment; protocol optimization; adaptive trials; predictive analytics

title: Integrating planetary health and environmental justice into high school construction career education: protocol for a randomized controlled trial of the Ecosystem Justice Translator
authors: Devan Cantrell Addison-Turner; Gretchen C. Daily
abstract: ABSTRACT Introduction Climate change disproportionately affects Disadvantaged Communities, yet construction workforce education rarely addresses interconnected pathways linking energy efficiency, nature exposure, and public health. Green-blue infrastructure delivers co-optimized benefits: reducing building energy consumption 15–30% while decreasing heat-related mortality by approximately 3.9% per degree Celsius of urban cooling (Gasparrini et al., 2017)— epidemiological benchmarks that inform the dose-response functions embedded in the Ecosystem Justice Translator (EJT). This protocol describes, to our knowledge, the first randomized controlled trial evaluating a curriculum intervention designed to develop planetary health competencies and environmental justice awareness among high school students pursuing construction careers. Methods and analysis This two-arm, parallel-group randomized controlled trial targets enrollment of N=200 high school students (ages 14–18) from construction career pathway programs in the San Francisco Bay Area (over-recruitment target N=250; 25% buffer for attrition). Students are individually randomized 1:1 to intervention (Community-Centered Design curriculum integrating the Ecosystem Justice Translator) or control (traditional Virtual Design and Construction curriculum), stratified by school site using block randomization. The 6-month intervention features the Ecosystem Justice Translator (EJT)—a computational system using large language models to translate community health equity concerns into quantifiable investment priorities. The EJT’s 51-theme health equity taxonomy was derived from validated public health frameworks (Centers for Disease Control and Prevention [CDC] Social Vulnerability Index, Environmental Protection Agency [EPA] EJScreen, Healthy People 2030). Primary outcome is Health-Integrated Equity Consciousness Index (HI-ECI), measured at baseline, 3, 6 (primary endpoint), and 12 months. Analysis uses intention-to-treat linear mixed-effects models with random intercepts for participants. The minimum required sample (n=26 per arm; G*Power, two-tailed α=0.05, 80% power, Hedges’ g=0.80) is exceeded by enrolled N=200, which provides >99% power at Hedges’ g=0.80 and supports multi-site confirmatory factor analysis. Ethics and dissemination This protocol has been approved by Stanford University Institutional Review Board (IRB eProtocol #84369, approved February 13, 2026). Parental consent from a parent or guardian and written assent from each student participant are required prior to enrollment. All instruments, curriculum materials, and EJT source code will be released open-source under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, permitting free use for educational, research, and non-profit purposes, concurrent with primary publication. Commercial licensing may be pursued separately through Stanford University Office of Technology Licensing (OTL docket S25-565). Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07315919 . Pre-results. Protocol version 4.1, July 2026. STRENGTHS AND LIMITATIONS OF THIS STUDY Individual randomization within school sites incorporates three structural contamination mitigations: mandatory active engagement with the intervention software, blinded outcome assessors, and temporal separation where the same instructor teaches both arms. A two-phase psychometric validation strategy—pilot exploratory factor analysis followed by confirmatory factor analysis with measurement invariance testing across school sites in the main trial—establishes the primary outcome’s factor structure and reliability. The single geographic context (San Francisco Bay Area) limits generalizability of findings to other regions and career technical education program structures. The primary and secondary outcome measures (HI-ECI and related indices) are novel and lack established normative benchmarks, so their psychometric properties will only be confirmed during the pilot phase. Curriculum delivery by trained career technical education instructors, rather than research team members, introduces fidelity variability that may attenuate observed effects relative to a tightly controlled efficacy trial.

title: The integration of large language models in clinical text analysis: A case study on dialysis vascular access descriptions
authors: Samuele Buosi; Finn Krewer; Luke Harris; Harsha Deswani; Harry Creagh; Maya Ganesan; George Mellotte; Prof. Joe Eustace; Conor S. Judge; Edward Curry
abstract: Structured data extraction is a key application of Large language Models (LLMs) which can enable quality improvement initiatives and answer research questions from routinely collected clinical data. We evaluated a pretrained LLM (Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct) for classifying vascular access routes from free text unstructured dialysis notes into either Central Venous Catheter (CVC) use and ArterioVenous Fistula (AVF), both or neither. Two independent binary tasks were defined on 1,990 clinician-annotated reports (AVF prevalence 11.7%; CVC 27.1%). We compared four prompting strategies—zero-shot, 4-shot, a recall-oriented “sensitive” structured question (SEN), and a precision-oriented “specific” structured question (SPE)—and measured accuracy, precision, recall, F1, and specificity. For CVC, zero-shot achieved F1 = 77.05% and 4-shot F1 = 79.85%. SEN increased recall (80.37%; precision 63.82%; F1 = 71.15%), whereas SPE achieved the highest precision (95.00%; recall 49.26%; F1 = 64.88%). For AVF, zero-shot yielded F1 = 55.40%; 4-shot raised recall (89.56%) with lower precision (25.43%; F1 = 39.62%); SPE provided the best balance (precision 81.36%; recall 62.07%; F1 = 70.42%). These results show that even smaller domain-agnostic LLMs can extract clinically meaningful signals from free text without fine-tuning, and that prompt design affords controllable sensitivity–specificity trade-offs aligned to different clinical objectives (e.g., case-finding vs registry curation). Prospective, multi-site validation and careful integration into clinical workflows are warranted to ensure safe and reliable deployment.

title: Faithful LLM-Assisted Question Answering for Technical and Academic Search
authors: Juan Luis Filgueiras
source_name: International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval (SIGIR)
abstract: Technology scouting and competitive intelligence increasingly rely on rapid access to scientific and technical evidence. Large language models (LLMs) are reshaping question answering by enabling users to express exploratory and evolving information needs in natural language. However, their usefulness is limited by hallucinations, weak calibration, poor abstention when evidence is missing, and the cost of keeping knowledge up to date. In such settings, the key question is whether LLM-generated answers can be trusted for decision support, that is, whether they are faithful to available evidence, transparent about uncertainty, and easy to verify. Recent work shows that hallucinations remain pervasive, while retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has become the main strategy for grounding answers in external evidence. Yet even strong RAG systems often cite unsupported claims or generate plausible but fabricated references, especially under poor retrieval conditions. In response, prior work has examined citation faithfulness, decomposed generations into checkable units, and proposed factuality verification models and benchmarks. Still, the literature underexplores how to filter and validate evidence when sources are sparse, conflicting, or rapidly changing, as is common in technical and academic search. This thesis addresses that gap by studying faithful LLM-assisted question answering for technical and academic search as an end-to-end problem spanning collection construction, model adaptation, grounded generation, evidence verification, and user-centered evaluation. It is organized around five questions: how LLMs can support exploratory search beyond keywords; how retrieval and generation pipelines can produce trustworthy responses; how systems should behave when evidence is sparse or unreliable; how usefulness and trustworthiness should be evaluated; and which architectures and optimization strategies enable reliable real-world deployment. The thesis argues that truthful technical search requires explicit mechanisms for claim-level grounding, calibrated abstention, contradiction handling, and support-aware evidence presentation. Methodologically, the work follows a pipeline perspective in which datasets, models, and evaluation procedures co-evolve. The empirical setup combines public QA and RAG benchmarks with technical and scientific collections tailored to technology scouting scenarios. A central methodological contribution will be the design of scenario-based evaluation subsets targeting null-retrieval, conflicting evidence, noisy or weak-signal evidence, and exploratory information needs. On top of these resources, the thesis will compare single-pass RAG and more structured agentic pipelines while varying retrieval strategies, prompting policies, claim-evidence alignment procedures, quotation and citation behaviors, and model adaptation techniques such as instruction tuning, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and reinforcement-based optimization. Evaluation will be multi-dimensional. In addition to answer utility and retrieval effectiveness, the thesis will measure citation faithfulness, support coverage, hallucination and false citation rates, abstention quality, uncertainty communication, and robustness under perturbed retrieval conditions. Whenever feasible, these automatic analyses will be complemented with analyst-oriented user studies that examine whether different evidence presentation formats help users reduce verification cost in realistic scouting workflows. Overall, the expected contribution is a principled and deployable framework for trustworthy natural-language access to scientific and technical information, combining faithful generation, verifiable evidence selection, and evaluation protocols tailored to real technical and academic search.

title: A Secondary-Data-Driven Decision Support Framework for Strategic Energy Investment Prioritization: An Explainable Multi-Criteria Application Across Countries
authors: Filiz Mızrak; Okan Yaşar
abstract: This study develops a secondary-data-driven decision support framework for prioritizing strategic energy investment readiness across countries. The empirical application covers 36 countries and 18 criteria grouped under macroeconomic feasibility, institutional capacity, energy security, sustainability and decarbonization, market and demand conditions, and technical resource potential. The study responds to a methodological gap in energy investment prioritization by moving from expert-only linguistic scoring toward a reproducible, explainable, stakeholder-sensitive, and validation-oriented multi-criteria decision support structure. In the implemented empirical model, public secondary data are transformed into a normalized country-level decision matrix, baseline readiness scores are calculated using equal weights, and entropy, Criteria Importance Through Intercriteria Correlation (CRITIC), and hybrid entropy-CRITIC configurations are used as objective weighting benchmarks. Large language model (LLM)-assisted extraction is used as a documented criterion-discovery and screening aid, not as an autonomous scoring, weighting, or ranking mechanism. The fuzzy component is specified as an uncertainty-sensitive extension and illustrated through panel-based fuzzy interval construction for selected time-series indicators, while the main baseline ranking is based on the latest available normalized data matrix. The results show meaningful cross-country variation, with top-10 readiness scores ranging from 0.675 to 0.537 and the lowest five scores ranging from 0.364 to 0.338. Persona-based results indicate that country priorities differ across public planners, private investors, grid operators, sustainability policymakers, and infrastructure funds, while robustness checks show broad ranking stability, with Spearman correlations between 0.892 and 0.986 and a median simulated-agent correlation of 0.932. Fairness and partial-correlation diagnostics suggest that the model captures multidimensional readiness rather than simply reproducing wealth or existing renewable capacity. Post-hoc validation against observable investment- and transition-related benchmarks further supports the convergent validity of the readiness index. The framework should therefore be interpreted as an early-stage country-level screening tool for strategic energy investment prioritization, not as a final project-level investment appraisal model.
