title: Bridging Proficiency Gaps: ChatGPT-Enhanced STAD for Achievement, Attitudes, and Equity in Multilingual Higher Education
authors: Yuheng Chen; Kimyung Keng
source_name: Journal of Information Technology Education Research
abstract: Aim/Purpose: This study examined whether embedding ChatGPT (GPT-4o) within Student Teams Achievement Divisions (STAD) cooperative learning improves academic achievement, learning attitudes, and interaction equity for linguistically heterogeneous undergraduates. Background: Linguistically diverse classrooms face an equity problem in which language proficiency operates as a status characteristic. Most existing AI-in-education studies report aggregate effects rather than subgroup outcomes, and few embed AI within structured cooperative architectures. Methodology: An 18-week quasi-experimental design with three time points was conducted at a Taiwanese university (N = 125; experimental n = 65, control n = 60). Participants were stratified by Test of Chinese as a Foreign Language (TOCFL) proficiency band, with Band A2 as the lower-proficiency threshold. The experimental condition followed a six-phase STAD workflow with tiered prompting and progressive scaffolding fading. Analyses included repeated-measures ANOVA, ANCOVA, and content analysis of reflection logs. Contribution: This study contributes (a) initial subgroup-level evidence, awaiting multi-site replication, that AI-enhanced STAD may narrow proficiency-based achievement gaps in content-area cooperative learning, (b) a replicable governance-embedded design, and (c) a theoretical extension positioning AI as a more knowledgeable other within the zone of proximal development. Findings: Five findings emerged. The experimental group exhibited steeper achievement growth (posttest d = 0.91). Four of six attitude dimensions improved significantly, led by Learning Confidence (d = 0.97). Self-reported prompting purposes differed substantially by proficiency subgroup (Cramér’s V = 0.37), with lower-proficiency learners reporting more language-clarification queries. The proficiency-based achievement gap narrowed from 16.60 to 4.00 points (Group × Proficiency partial η² = 0.050). Exploratory and preliminary evidence further suggested that female students reported higher residual subject anxiety than male students. However, this finding did not survive Bonferroni correction and is constrained by low subscale reliability. Recommendations for Practitioners: Practitioners should embed AI access at specific interaction nodes, differentiate scaffolding through tiered prompts, govern AI use through written agreements and reflection logs, plan progressive fading, and monitor affective outcomes for vulnerable subgroups. Impact on Society: The equity evidence suggests that blanket AI prohibitions may inadvertently disadvantage linguistically diverse learners. The governance-embedded design offers an adaptable model for institutional and national AI-use policies. Future Research: Future research should deploy automated, timestamped AI usage logs; replicate across institutions and disciplines; revise low-reliability subscales using rigorous CFA on larger samples (N ≥ 300); and conduct longitudinal follow-up to assess persistence of equity effects.

title: Public Sports Facility Location Planning Based on LLM-Enhanced Deep Transfer Optimization
authors: Lu Chen; Si Chen
source_name: IEICE Transactions on Fundamentals of Electronics Communications and Computer Sciences
abstract: With the improvement of urban public service systems, selecting sites for public sports facilities is essential for enhancing well-being and promoting spatial equity. However, existing spatial statistical and optimization methods struggle to interpret policy semantics, address regional data gaps, and balance multiple objectives, leading to poor policy consistency and limited generalizability. This study proposes a large language-model-enhanced deep transfer optimization (LDTO) framework that integrates LLM-based semantic parsing with deep spatial representation learning through a Semantic-Spatial Collaborative Alignment mechanism. A cross-regional adaptive transfer module strengthens robustness in data-scarce areas via adversarial alignment and meta-parameter updating. A dynamic multi-objective reinforcement learning strategy further enables adaptive balancing of coverage, cost, and equity. Experiments show that LDTO significantly improves policy consistency, transferability, and multi-objective coordination, offering a new paradigm that fuses semantic understanding with spatial optimization for equitable urban governance.

title: GENERATIVE AI FOR SUPPLY CHAIN OPTIMIZATION: OPPORTUNITIES AND ETHICAL RISKS IN PROCUREMENT
authors: Godspower Onyekachukwu Ekwueme
abstract: The introduction of Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) technology in supply chain management has facilitated the automation of procurement processes, supplier selection, optimization of inventory management and demand forecasting among other benefits. However, the use of Generative AI in procurement processes brings forth several ethical issues including transparency, algorithmic biases, data privacy and security, accountability and displacement of jobs. This study focused on investigating the opportunities and ethical dilemmas posed using Generative AI technology in supply chain optimization, particularly procurement process. The research employed a qualitative approach through the content analysis of academic journals. The secondary data used in the study includes journal articles, conference papers, industrial reports, and policy documents. It is found out that Generative AI technology is highly efficient in improving procurement through intelligent supplier assessment, contract creation, predictive analysis, demand forecasting, inventory optimization, and real-time decision-making processes. On the other hand, the findings suggest that poor governance frameworks, low data quality, algorithm discrimination, lack of transparency, cyber-security threats, and ethical issues associated with accountability can jeopardize the sustainable implementation of the technology. It can be concluded that the incorporation of Generative Artificial Intelligence in supply chain management has many advantages ranging from increased efficiency to better decision-making capabilities, forecasting accuracy, procurement activities, and increased resilience. Unfortunately, there are various challenges facing companies in Nigeria that limit the ability to incorporate generative artificial intelligence in supply chain management.

title: Adversarial Agentic LLM based optimization for factory layout and dispatching selection
authors: Johannes Pflüger; Wei Ye; Xingyu Li; Sang-Gook Kim; Marvin Carl May
abstract: Heuristic methods remain vital for production scheduling and dispatching, yet manual design limits adaptability. This work introduces the Adversarial Agent-Based Large Language Model Evolutionary Algorithm (LLaMEA) Framework, integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) into evolutionary optimization to autonomously generate and refine heuristic strategies. A dual-agent workflow proposes and evaluates production strategies through iterative improvement. Evolutionary operators combined with LLM-driven reasoning to evolve interpretable solutions in simulation-based environments. A persistent archive captures successful solutions across optimization runs, enabling knowledge transfer and accelerating convergence in new tasks. This knowledge-driven mechanism distinguishes the approach from purely generative methods through contextual adaptation of accumulated expertise. Validation on a matrix production benchmark confirms LLM-generated strategies achieve Pareto-optimal performance comparable to genetic algorithms while maintaining transparency and requiring significantly less manual effort, establishing a scalable foundation for adaptive production optimization.

title: End-to-End Architecture for LLM-Based Business Process Automation: A Low-Code Integration Framework With Performance Benchmarking
authors: Rajesh Soma
abstract: Intelligent decision-making remains a major gap in traditional Business Process Management (BPM) systems, which are typically limited to rule-based workflows and require human intervention for complex decisions. This paper introduces LLMFlow, a novel low-code integration framework that connects large language models (LLMs), such as GPT-4, with the Microsoft Power Platform to deliver intelligent, end-to-end business process automation. LLMFlow was evaluated across three enterprise deployments: invoice processing, customer service automation, and supply chain optimization, achieving 92% processing accuracy, 62% faster response times, and 53% lower operational costs per transaction compared to traditional BPM solutions. The system sustained 132 requests per second, with a consistent average response time of 456 ms. To our knowledge, this work presents one of the early production-validated implementations of a multi-LLM orchestration framework that integrates predictive response-time routing with low-code workflow compilation and enterprise benchmarking.

title: Privacy-enhancing methodologies and privacy risk discovery in neuroimaging data: From differentially private distribution estimation and visualization to brain foundation model evaluation
authors: Ye Tao
abstract: Privacy protection has become increasingly important in data science and is especially critical in neuroimaging, where limited data at individual sites often motivates multi-site collaboration. Sharing data in such settings typically involves cumbersome and time-consuming approval procedures. Differential privacy (DP) provides a systematic framework for data sharing while balancing privacy and utility. In this dissertation, we introduce novel methods for distribution approximation and visualization under differential privacy. We also investigate the use of large-scale pre-trained models to obtain compact representations of fMRI data, assessing both their utility for downstream analyses and the risk of exposing batch information. We first focus on privacy-preserving distribution approximation. The cumulative distribution function (CDF) is fundamental for characterizing random variables, making it a key tool in privacy-preserving analysis. We introduce a novel framework for constructing differentially private CDFs inspired by functional analysis and the functional mechanism. Two variants are developed: a polynomial projection method, which projects the empirical CDF into a polynomial space, and a sparse approximation method via matching pursuit, which projects it into arbitrary function spaces constructed from dictionaries. In both cases, the empirical CDF is approximated within the chosen space, and the corresponding coefficients are privatized to guarantee differential privacy. Compared with existing approaches such as histogram queries and adaptive quantiles, our methods achieve comparable or superior performance. They are particularly well-suited to decentralized settings and scenarios where CDFs must be efficiently updated with newly collected or streaming data. We also investigate the impact of parameters such as dictionary size and systematically evaluate different dictionary constructions, including Legendre polynomials, B-splines, and distribution-based functions. Beyond protecting data, visualizations can themselves reveal sensitive information; for example, individual values can be inferred directly from boxplots or scatterplots. Privacy-preserving visualizations can be categorized into two types. The first type relies on synthetic data generated from differentially private distribution approximation, which allows downstream analyses without accessing raw data. However, producing accurate approximations is particularly challenging in high-dimensional settings. The second type applies privacy-preserving techniques directly to visual representations derived from the data. While existing differential privacy methods are well-established for numerical data, it remains unclear whether they can be directly adapted to visual representations, as preserving the information conveyed by the original visualization may require different considerations. This motivates our investigation of DP visualization techniques. We focus on neuroimaging analyses of functional network connectivity (FNC), exploring several perturbation-based approaches to correlation values and characterizing their privacy costs as well as pre- and post-processing impacts. To improve the tradeoff between privacy and visual utility, we propose workflows for connectogram and seed-based connectivity visualizations, which produce results similar to their non-private counterparts. Experimental results demonstrate that these methods preserve the information conveyed by the original visualization while ensuring privacy, highlighting the potential of differential privacy for secure and informative visual analytics. We also investigate the use of large-scale pre-trained models to obtain compact embeddings of functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data, which may facilitate multi-site analyses without exchanging high-dimensional raw scans. Using embeddings generated by BrainLM and SwiFT across multiple datasets, including FBIRN, ADHD-200, and ABIDE I, we evaluate their properties using both qualitative methods such as PCA and LDA and quantitative approaches including PERMANOVA and classification models for site and diagnostic labels. Our results indicate that while these embeddings encode clinically relevant signals, they are strongly influenced by batch effects, which can dominate over subtle diagnostic information and reveal batch membership. Ridge regression analyses predicting brain measures such as ALFF and FNC further show that BrainLM embeddings are particularly sensitive to regional activity, whereas SwiFT embeddings preferentially capture functional connectivity patterns. These findings illustrate the dual nature of foundation model embeddings: they provide powerful, compact representations that capture meaningful brain information while simultaneously carrying non-negligible signals that could expose batch characteristics. To summarize, this dissertation presents privacy-aware neuroimaging analyses in three complementary directions. We develop novel and efficient differentially private methods for distribution approximation. We design differentially private visualization techniques that preserve the information conveyed by the original visualizations while controlling privacy risks. Finally, we evaluate large-scale pre-trained foundation models, showing that compact embeddings can capture meaningful brain information, but they can also unintentionally reveal batch membership.

title: LLM-Guided Exemplar Selection for Few-Shot Wearable-Sensor Human Activity Recognition
authors: Ronando Elsen; Sozo Inoue
abstract: In this paper, we introduce an LLM-Guided Exemplar Selection framework to address a key limitation in state-of-the-art Human Activity Recognition (HAR) methods: their reliance on large labeled datasets and purely geometric exemplar selection, which often fail to distinguish similar wearable sensor activities such as walking, walking upstairs, and walking downstairs. Our method incorporates semantic reasoning via an LLM-generated knowledge prior that captures feature importance, inter-class confusability, and exemplar budget multipliers, and uses it to guide exemplar scoring and selection. These priors are integrated with margin-based validation cues, PageRank centrality, hubness penalization, and facility-location optimization to obtain a compact and informative set of exemplars. Evaluated on the UCI-HAR dataset under strict few-shot conditions, the framework achieves a mean macro F1-score of +10.36%, outperforming classical approaches such as random sampling. The results show that LLM-derived semantic priors, when integrated with structural and geometric cues, can provide a stronger foundation for selecting representative sensor exemplars within few-shot wearable-sensor HAR settings.

title: ARCS: Adversarial RF Map Categorization and Synthesis Through Unsupervised Feature Extraction
authors: Sopan Sarkar; Marwan Krunz; David Manzi; R S Kulkarni
source_name: IEEE Transactions on Machine Learning in Communications and Networking
abstract: In wireless networks, radio-frequency coverage maps (RF maps) are critical for tasks such as capacity planning, coverage estimation, and localization. Traditional methods for obtaining these maps, including site surveys and ray-tracing simulations, are either labor-intensive or computationally expensive, particularly at high frequencies. Generative AI offers a promising alternative for RF map synthesis and data augmentation. However, supervised generative approaches are often infeasible due to the lack of labeled training data, while unsupervised methods typically lack control over the generation process, limiting their practical utility. To overcome these challenges, we propose ARCS (Adversarial RF Map Categorization and Synthesis), a novel generative adversarial network (GAN)-based framework for unsupervised RF map categorization and synthesis. ARCS leverages the principles of information maximizing GAN (InfoGAN) to learn the latent structure of RF maps in an unsupervised manner during training and, through manipulation of the learned and interpretable latent codes, enables controlled generation of RF maps across floor-plan regions and Tx locations during inference. To improve training stability and synthesis quality, we integrate a gradient penalty-based Wasserstein GAN objective function along with a customized gradient-based loss function. Extensive experiments on both experimental and simulated datasets show that ARCS generates high-quality RF maps, associates them with discrete regions of the floor plan, and provides fine-grained control of Tx location within each region. Compared with a UNet-based conditional GAN and a conditional diffusion model, ARCS attains the best scores across structural similarity index metric (SSIM), PSNR, MAPE, RMSE, cosine similarity (CS), and Jensen–Shannon divergence (JSD). Moreover, ARCS is extremely fast, requiring a few milliseconds per synthetic map, compared to over 14 seconds with ray-tracing.

title: Artificial Intelligence Driven Product Development: An analysis of how the integration of Artificial Intelligence into the automotive development process can shorten the product development cycle
authors: Eduan Howard
abstract: This thesis explores the transformative potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in accelerating product development cycles within the automotive industry, amid rapid shifts toward electric vehicles (EVs) and sustainable mobility. As global competition intensifies—driven by market leaders like Tesla and Chinese OEMs such as BYD—traditional development processes face challenges in speed, e!ciency, and innovation. The study hypothesizes that integrating AI into key stages of the automotive product lifecycle management (PLM) can reduce developmenttimelines by 20-50%, enhancing competitiveness through optimized workflows and resource allocation. Building on a comprehensive literature review of PLM, technology innovation management, systems engineering models (e.g., V-Model and MBSE), and AI advancements, the methodology proposes a departmentalized AI agent structure tailored to automotive contexts. This includes Future Innovation (7-10 year horizon) for technology scouting, Research & Development (4-7years) for design exploration, and Serial Development (2-4 years) for production maturation. A practical case study on electric traction drive development illustrates AI’s role in requirement refinement, trade-o" analysis, and simulation, yielding significant time savings while maintaining focus on business outcomes like cost reduction and market agility. Key findings demonstrate that AI-driven processes, such as generative AI for ideation and model-based engineering for validation, can streamline the innovation funnel, mitigate risks in chaotic technology landscapes (via adapted Stacey Matrix), and support generational product pulls. Implications for the automotive sector include improved margins (up to 5% uplift per PwC insights), faster time-to-market, and strategic advantages in the EV transition. imitations include reliance on hypothetical scenarios and ethical AI considerations, with recommendations for future work emphasizing real-world implementations and workforce upskilling. Overall, this research underscores AI as a strategic enabler for automotive firms to thrive in a dynamic, technology-push environment.

title: A Neural Network‐Based Decision Framework Utilizing Large Language Models and Neutrosophic Sets for Sustainable Supplier Selection
authors: Amirhossein Nafei; Zhi Li; S. Pourmohammad Azizi
abstract: Sustainable supplier selection is a high‐impact decision problem in which organizations must jointly evaluate economic performance, environmental impact, and social responsibility under heterogeneous stakeholder preferences, asymmetric decision authority, and predominantly linguistic assessments. Conventional multiattribute group decision‐making (MAGDM) methods, based on crisp scores, fixed aggregation rules, and implicit consensus are poorly suited to contexts where expert opinions are expressed in natural language, indeterminacy is substantial, and strategic priorities may override majority preferences. To address these limitations, this study proposes a neural‐based decision framework that integrates large language models (LLMs), neutrosophic sets, an autocratic aggregation strategy, and a neural network for supplier selection. Criterion‐specific textual judgments provided by experts are processed by a pretrained model to extract sentiment polarity and confidence, which are then mapped to neutrosophic triplets. An autocratic mechanism empowers a designated decision leader to choose context‐appropriate scoring and aggregation functions, avoiding forced consensus and reducing the need for extensive pairwise comparisons. A neural aggregation layer further learns how to combine multiple neutrosophic score functions, refining ranking behavior and lowering computational complexity. The framework is validated through a case study on sustainable supplier selection. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach produces stable, interpretable rankings with reduced computational burden and closer alignment with strategic sustainability goals than benchmark MAGDM methods.

title: GenAI-CDS and Clinical Reasoning Development in Pre-Clinical Medical Education
authors: Michael B. Moore
abstract: This project houses a research program investigating how generative AI clinical decision support (GenAI-CDS) affects clinical reasoning development in pre-clinical medical students. The program is grounded in Cognitive Load Theory (CLT), the CHART+M behavioral assessment framework, and the Siden input typology extended to pre-clinical learners. The central theoretical contribution is the "never-skilling" hypothesis: that AI access during formative training may prevent foundational schema formation entirely, a mechanism distinct from the deskilling documented in experienced clinicians. The program spans three domains. First, a randomized simulation study testing whether GenAI-CDS access during acute care simulation supports or undermines transfer performance on AI-absent key-feature examinations (funded by NBOME). Second, SAFE-CRS (Scaffolded AI Framework for Evidence-Based Clinical Reasoning in Simulation), a multi-site implementation targeting academic medical partnerships in low- and middle-income countries. Third, dissemination through workshops, peer-reviewed publications, and public scholarship translating findings for medical educators and policymakers. The key-feature examination and licensure board examination (COMLEX-USA, COMAT) function as structural equalizers in this program. Both are AI-absent, standardized, and consequential. They operationalize the never-skilling hypothesis at the individual study level and at population scale, respectively.

title: CALM: Cycle-Aware Latent Modeling for Arteriovenous Fistula Assessment Using Audio Foundation Models and Low-Level Descriptors
authors: Whenty Ariyanti; Ping-Yi Lin; Chia-Yu Hu; Shang‐Feng Yang; Shin-Hung Tsai; Li-Ning Peng; Huang Ph; Hsin‐Min Wang; Yu Tsao
source_name: IEEE Journal of Translational Engineering in Health and Medicine
abstract: Objective: Arteriovenous fistula (AVF) dysfunction is a major cause of morbidity in hemodialysis (HD) patients. Although conventional monitoring tools are clinically effective, they are often limited by cost, invasiveness, and operator dependence. This study proposes a cycle-aware, auscultation-based deep learning framework for objective and scalable assessment of AVF blood flow status. Methods and Procedures: We developed CALM, a physiologically informed learning framework that integrates Hilbert-based cycle segmentation with pretrained audio foundation model (AFM) representations. A clinical auscultation dataset (CHGH-AVF) from 188 HD patients at three standardized vascular access sites was collected and labeled using concurrent blood flow measurements. The proposed approach was evaluated on both three-class flow-severity classification (Low, Medium, and High) and binary flow-quality screening (Ideal vs. Unideal). Model variants incorporating domain-specific low-level descriptors and different feature fusion strategies were also investigated. Results: Across all auscultation sites, CALM consistently outperformed conventional handcrafted-feature baselines, deep learning baselines, and classical machine learning-based classifiers in patient-level flow-severity classification. Ablation studies demonstrated that physiologic cycle segmentation substantially improves discriminability, while integrating complementary low-level descriptors (LLDs) further enhanced performance across anatomically different recording locations. Although classification performance remained highest at the proximal sites, reduced performance at the venous site highlighted the influence of anatomical location and signal quality. Strong performance was also observed for binary flow-quality monitoring, particularly at the proximal auscultation sites. Conclusion: The proposed framework demonstrates the feasibility of AFM–based auscultation for non-invasive AVF flow assessment. By combining physiologic signal modeling with foundation model representations, CALM provides a robust and objective framework for automated assessment of vascular access function.Clinical Impact: This work introduces a multi-site clinical AVF auscultation dataset and establishes automated auscultation analysis as a low-cost and scalable adjunct to existing vascular access monitoring practices in HD care.Clinical and Translational Impact Statement: AFM-based auscultation has the potential to support objective screening of AVF dysfunction and may facilitate future integration into bedside or home monitoring systems, enabling more accessible and scalable vascular access monitoring.

title: Essays on the Labor economics of automation and AI
authors: Christian Gschwendt
source_name: Open Access CRIS of the University of Bern
abstract: This dissertation provides novel evidence on how recent advances in automation and AI technology influence active workers' assessments of automation risk, future workers' occupational preferences and choices, and firms' training decisions. This dissertation has been fundamentally defined by the emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), as every project within it—directly or indirectly—revolves around its implications. What makes this new technology so profoundly disruptive? In all four chapters, I empirically investigate perceptions of and responses to GenAI in the Swiss labor market. Switzerland—ranking first in global innovation with a highly skilled workforce and strong GenAI potential—also features a distinctive dual-education system, where adolescents make early career choices, and firms deliver entry-level training for two thirds of future workers, making it an ideal setting to study imminent GenAI effects on workers' and firms' human capital investments. In Chapters 1, 3, and 4, we use primary data from large-scale experiments specifically designed to address each of the studies' research questions: How do active workers assess the risk of automation, and what are they willing to pay to reduce this risk? How do training firms plan to adjust their entry-level training positions in response to GenAI-driven automation prospects? And how do future workers evaluate GenAI collaboration in their future occupations? In Chapter 2, we use search query data to examine how the unanticipated launch of ChatGPT has affected the occupational choices of labor market entrants.

title: Benchmarking Commercial Speech Recognition and Multimodal Large Language Models on Dysarthric Speech: Severity‐Stratified Baselines and Architecture‐Specific Prompting Effects
authors: Ali Alsayegh; Tariq Masood
abstract: Voice‐based human‐machine interaction has become a primary means of accessing intelligent systems, yet individuals with dysarthria are systematically excluded by persistent gaps in recognition accuracy. Whilst automatic speech recognition (ASR) achieves word error rates (WER) below 5% on typical speech, performance degrades sharply for dysarthric speakers; and although multimodal large language models (MLLMs) might compensate for acoustic degradation through contextual reasoning, their zero‐shot behaviour on such speech remains uncharacterised. To address this, we evaluate eight commercial speech‐to‐text services on the TORGO dysarthric speech corpus, comprising four conventional ASR systems (AssemblyAI, Whisper large‐v3, Deepgram Nova‐3 and Nova‐3 Medical) and four MLLM‐based systems (GPT‐4o, GPT‐4o Mini, Gemini 2.5 Pro and Gemini 2.5 Flash), across lexical accuracy, semantic preservation and cost‐latency trade‐offs. Recognition degraded consistently with severity: mild dysarthria reached low single‐digit WER, around 1% to 2% for the leading systems, approaching typical‐speech benchmarks, whereas severe dysarthria exceeded 51% WER for every system, with the MLLMs offering no advantage over conventional ASR at this tier under default settings. A four‐condition prompt ablation revealed strongly architecture‐specific effects, whereby, for the OpenAI multimodal models, any verbatim‐transcription prompt reduced severe‐tier WER mainly by suppressing nontarget‐language drift, lowering GPT‐4o from 60.1% to 52.9% and GPT‐4o Mini from 66.0% to roughly 55%, with the three prompt variants performing similarly; the Gemini models, which did not exhibit this failure mode to the same extent, showed no consistent benefit and sometimes degraded. title: The Impact of AI on the Labour Market : Essays on Transformative Technology, Occupations, and Firms
authors: Erik Engberg
source_name: KTH Publication Database DiVA (KTH Royal Institute of Technology)
abstract: The topic of this thesis is the economics of transformative technology, with the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on the labour market as the primary focus. Analysing German data, Essay I shows that occupational AI exposure was associated with wage gains, and an increased focus on knowledge-intensive tasks. There is a clear contrast between the types of work that are exposed to AI, versus robotics. Essay II finds that AI exposure is associated with AI adoption and increased labour demand, as measured by job vacancy postings, in Swedish establishments/workplaces. Essay III develops a novel measure of occupational AI exposure, called Dynamic AI Occupational Exposure (DAIOE). AI exposure is shown to be associated with upskilling at the firm level in Sweden, Denmark, and Portugal. Essay IV analyses the labour market implications of the growing social and verbal capabilities of large language models (LLMs). Analysis of occupational data from O*NET and job ads provides a map of the most important types of social work tasks. Among social tasks, verbal communication tasks have the strongest association with occupational exposure to LLMs. Essay V is about the impact of venture capital (VC) on start-up firms. Investment from both private and governmental VCs is found to increase sales with a 2-3 year delay, driven primarily by efficiency gains, and to some extent, capital investment. Governmental VCs are more likely to make follow-on investments in non-growing firms.

title: Automatic model generation for discrete-event simulation
authors: Sanket Kute; Sebastian Lang
source_name: Digitalen Hochschulbibliothek Sachsen-Anhalt (Universitäts- und Landesbibliothek Sachsen-Anhalt)
abstract: Automatic model generation for manufacturing- oriented discrete-event simulation (DES) aims to reduce the effort required to build and update material flow and production system models. Established automatic simulation model generation (ASMG) approaches often rely on structured engineering data, event logs, or predefined transformation logic. Recent progress in large language models creates new opportunities to use less formalized information, including textual planning notes, layout descriptions, process assumptions, and parameter tables. However, current LLM-assisted approaches still face limitations in reliability, transparency, reproducibility, and simulator integration. This paper derives a conceptual framework for LLM- assisted automatic model generation in manufacturing-oriented discrete-event simulation. The proposed workflow combines hybrid information extraction, a simulation-oriented intermediate representation, explicit validation, simulator-specific instantiation, and expert review. The LLM is positioned as a controlled component for semantic interpretation and structuring, not as an autonomous end-to-end model generator. Particular attention is given to behavioural and control-related aspects because these are required for executable and useful manufacturing simulation models. The paper concludes by outlining a phased prototype implementation and evaluation strategy using controlled manufacturing use cases and later validation with an industrial factory-planning partner.

title: Generative AI Literacy Among Indian Secondary-School Students: Awareness, Usage, Verification and Risk Perception
authors: Aryaveer Singh
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools can produce fluent explanations, summaries, images, code, and answers, but fluent output is not necessarily accurate, unbiased, private, or educationally appropriate. For secondary-school students, meaningful literacy therefore extends beyond awareness or frequency of use. It includes functional understanding, purposeful use, critical verification, calibrated trust, recognition of risk, and responsible behaviour. This paper develops an academically grounded protocol for investigating these dimensions among students in Classes IX and X in India. The proposed cross-sectional, multi-site survey uses a mixed-format instrument combining objective knowledge items, self-reported competence, behavioural-frequency measures, and scenario-based verification tasks. The conceptual model treats GenAI literacy as five related constructs: functional AI understanding, applied AI competence, critical evaluation and verification, risk and ethical awareness, and responsible AI behaviour. Access, school context, language, prior instruction, and usage patterns are treated as contextual predictors, while trust is examined as a calibration variable rather than as an uncomplicated indicator of literacy. The protocol specifies a realistic independent-student sampling strategy, pilot testing, translation procedures, content and construct validation, reliability analysis, ethical safeguards for minors, and an analysis plan that accounts for clustering and multiple comparisons. It also supplies participant materials, a complete draft questionnaire, and a variable-coding framework. No empirical findings are reported because primary data have not yet been collected. The study is designed to produce transparent, reproducible evidence about how Indian secondary-school students use GenAI, how they judge its outputs, and what forms of school-based instruction could strengthen safe, critical, and responsible use.

title: Zero-Shot Multi-Reference Personalization via MLLMs-Guided Layout Planning
authors: Junhao Feng
abstract: Though zero-shot adapters excel in image personalization, they often encounter significant challenges in multi-reference personalized generation, specifically failing to precisely adhere to the spatial layouts described in text prompts and suffering from feature leakage between reference images. To address these two challenges, we propose RIG (Regional Image-prompt Generation), a novel training-free framework. For the first challenge, leveraging Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), we introduce a layout planning binder. Leveraging Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning, this module infers and generates precise global layouts from text prompts, while simultaneously binding reference images to their corresponding regions. For the second, we introduce a satially decoupled diffusion mechanism that isolates feature streams during attention computation. By injecting reference features exclusively into designated regions, this mechanism effectively prevents feature interference between reference images. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RIG significantly outperforms state-of-the-art adapter methods in terms of both personalization fidelity and text-layout alignment.

title: Enabling Human-AI Collaboration in a Modular Planning Environment
authors: Esben Schukat; Lea Röhm; Markus Netzer; Güther Schuh
source_name: Institutional Repository of Leibniz Universität Hannover (Leibniz Universität Hannover)
abstract: The vision of fully automated factory planning remains an elusive goal. The complexity and context-dependency of tasks in factory panning still demand human expertise. This paper introduces the concept of a Factory Planning Copilot, which shifts the focus from automation to intelligent assistance. Inspired by systems like Microsoft Copilot, the approach envisions a virtual environment where planners interact with digital factory models through natural language, supported by large language models. Rather than replacing human judgment, the Copilot augments it by interpreting intentions, suggesting improvements, and enabling intuitive access to complex planning data. By embedding domain knowledge through modular expert systems and fostering an open ecosystem, the Copilot can accelerate planning processes, enhance decision quality, and improve compliance with internal and external requirements. Copilot for Factory Planning aims to make digital factory planning more accessible, adaptive, and reliable to empower planners through seamless human-AI collaboration.

abstract: Pre-registration Perceptions of LLM models Study 2 Human-GenAI Cooperation: From Descriptions of AI Partners to Impression Formation to Cooperation Study 2 Questions 1) How do people perceive different existing LLM chatbots (and other humans) and how does an interaction influence perceptions? 2) How do different existing LLM chatbots perceive themselves and other chatbots (and humans)? We conduct an experiment consisting of two parts. In the first part, humans indicate their perceptions of different prominent AI chatbots (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, Grok, DeepSeek, Qwen, and Le Chat; as well as a human), interact with a chatbot in a prisoner’s dilemma, and again indicate their perceptions of the chatbot they interacted with. In the second part, the same AI chatbots will be prompted to indicate their perceptions of themselves, the other chatbots, and a human from a representative sample of the US. The goals of this study are to (1) map how people perceive different real-world chatbots (vs humans) in terms of person perception and mind perception; (2) map how real-world LLM chatbots perceive themselves and different chatbots (vs humans) in terms of person perception and mind perception, (3) compare the perceptions of humans and LLM chatbots, and (4) test hypotheses regarding perceptions, interactions with chatbots, and reputation-based cooperation. Conditions Presented LLMs: Human participants will be randomly presented with 4 out of 8 LLMs to evaluate (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, Grok, DeepSeek, Qwen, and Le Chat). Models will be presented with the company that has developped them and the country in which that company is based. LLM Chatbots will rate all 8 LLMs (including themselves). LLM cooperation: Participants will be presented with cooperation or defection by 1 randomly selected LLM in a prisoner’s dilemma. The probability of encountering cooperation versus defection will be set by initially prompting each LLM for their decision in the prisoner’s dilemma a minimum of 500 times and setting the percentage of cooperation across those responses as the cooperation rate. LLM chatbots will not be presented these conditions. Presented human to rate: Participants will be randomly presented with 1 out of 4 human interactions partners to rate (random person drawn from a representative sample of the US, colleague, friend, romantic partner). LLM Chatbots will always rate a person (human). Dependent variables Person perception: (1) Horizontal dimension facet friendliness: composite score ranging from 1 (low) to 7 (high) (2) Horizontal dimension facet morality: composite score ranging from 1 (low) to 7 (high) The above measures are combined into index of horizontal person perception. This is measured before and after the interaction with the LLM. LLM chatbots will be prompted to answer each item X times for each LLM they rate. (3) Vertical dimension facet ability: composite score ranging from 1 (low) to 7 (high) (4) Vertical dimension facet assertiveness: composite score ranging from 1 (low) to 7 (high) The above measures are combined into index of vertical person perception. LLM chatbots were prompted to answer each item a minimum of 500 times for each LLM they rate. Mind perception: (1) Dimension Experience: composite score ranging from 1 (low) to 7 (high) (2) Dimension Agency: composite score ranging from 1 (low) to 7 (high) This is measured before and after the interaction with the LLM. LLM chatbots were prompted to answer each item a minimum of 500 times for each LLM they rate. Cooperation: (1) Cooperation in a prisoner’s dilemma: cooperate (1) versus defect (0). LLM chatbots were prompted to answer each item a minimum of 500 times for each LLM they rate. To rate their cooperation with human participants, each LLM will be prompted for their decision in the prisoner’s dilemma a minimum of 500 times to get a cooperation rate. Partner selection: (1) Selection as partner in a second prisoner’s dilemma: selected or not from a list with the 4 presented LLMs. LLM Chatbots do not do this measure. Hypotheses H1: We expect that experiencing cooperation (defection) from an LLM to be positively (negatively) correlated with cooperation and partner selection in the prisoner’s dilemma as well as with increased (reduced) perceptions of warmth H2: We expect that initial perceptions of warmth in LLMs to be positively correlated with cooperation and partner selection in the prisoner’s dilemma H3: We expect that initial perceptions of competence in LLMs to be positively correlated with cooperation and partner selection in the prisoner’s dilemma H4: We expect that the correlation between initial perceptions of warmth correlated with cooperation and partner selection in the prisoner’s dilemma is stronger than the correlations for initial perceptions of competence H5: We expect that initial perceptions of experience in LLMs to be positively correlated with cooperation and partner selection Analyses We will use mixed effects linear regression models and multilevel correlation analyses. Outliers and Exclusions We will exclude from analyses participants who fail any of four attention checks: (1) during the perception questionnaire participants must select a specific answer option four times, for the first LLM evaluation, the last LLM evaluation, during the person perception task, and when evaluating an average other participant. Participants who fail these attention checks are not eligible for a bonus payment of $0.15 nor the bonus from the prisoner’s dilemmas. We will further exclude from analyses participants who are suspected of being or using bots by including a white text on white background (i.e., invisible to human participants) asking to report their favorite ice cream flavor at the end of the study. Participants who report this will be excluded from analyses. Further to complete the study, participants must (1) pass an image selection CAPTCHA prior to the study if their reCAPTCHA score is lower than 0.7, and (2) pass an image selection CAPTCHA after completing the perceptions evaluations for two LLMs. Sample Size Based on available resources, we aim for each the 8 selected LLMs to be evaluated at least 400 times. Since each participant rates 4 LLMs, this requires a minimum of 800 participants. LLMs will be prompted a minimum of 500 times times for rating themselves, each other model, and a human. Other We will further explore the roles of measure familiarity with each presented LLM (1 = never heard of it, 7 = use it frequently), knowledge of LLMS (rated on two multiple choice items about what LLMs are and do), usage of LLMs in different roles (select how they use the presented LLMs) and expected cooperation in the prisoner’s dilemma by the selected other (cooperate versus defect) in perception and partner selection. We will also explore comparisons of perceptions and benchmarks of LLM models. Given sensitivity to instructions for LLMs, we will potentially run additional trials of LLM ratings and cooperation after the study.

title: Skill-based and Hardware-Independent Control for Robots using Natural Language Task Description
authors: Niklas Bönisch; Adrian Reuther; Benjamin Schleich
abstract: The increasing complexity of manufacturing systems, coupled with the trend of smaller production lot sizes, makes it exceedingly difficult for companies to design and configure these systems. This is because designing and configuring flexible manufacturing systems requires detailed knowledge of the systems themselves, which presents a significant challenge, particularly for SMEs lacking the necessary expertise. This paper proposes a novel approach that derives skill sequences based on a natural language task description to ease manufacturing system design and configuration. It employs a large language model (LLM) to process natural language input, which utilizes the novel Model Context Protocol to gather relevant manufacturing system information as well as the Open Platforms Communications Unified Architecture (OPC UA) communication standard and its companion specifications. By doing so, it retrieves information about available skills and their descriptions. Based on user input and the OPC UA information model, the approach generates a skill sequence for the flexible manufacturing system. Using an LLM enables an integrated feedback loop, allowing users to clarify the process and refine the generated outcome. Consequently, the LLM can execute the derived skill sequence via the OPC UA interface. This approach bridges the gap between natural language user input and the system control in manufacturing systems. The functionality is demonstrated using one articulated robot that is controlled via OPC UA. As such, the paper introduces a novel solution for configuring flexible manufacturing systems using natural language, eliminating the need for detailed knowledge of a specific system. This approach lays the foundation for more user friendly, accessible, and expert-independent configuration of flexible manufacturing systems.

title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on American and Canadian Hospitals' Internal Functioning and Patient Outcomes: A Systematic Review
authors: Ahmed Elsayed
abstract: Primary purpose: This systematic review aims to synthesize the available evidence on artificial intelligence (AI) initiatives implemented in American and Canadian hospitals between September 2022 and August 2024, and to assess the impact of these initiatives on hospitals' internal functioning and patients' medical outcomes. Why this is needed: Three gaps in the existing literature motivated this review. First, no systematic review has compared AI implementation across the United States and Canada simultaneously, despite both countries being global leaders in healthcare AI adoption—the US as the largest investor and patent holder (GlobalData, 2024), and Canada as the first country with a national AI strategy affecting healthcare (Radu, 2021). Second, prior systematic reviews on AI in healthcare (Meskó et al., 2018; Choudhury & Asan, 2020; Obermeyer & Emanuel, 2016) predate the 2022 peak in FDA-approved AI/ML medical devices (Joshi et al., 2024) and therefore do not capture the current regulatory and deployment landscape. Third, the specific impact of AI on hospitals' internal functioning—as opposed to patient outcomes alone—has not been systematically examined as a primary outcome domain.Specific objectives: Objective Description Objective 1 Identify and categorize the main AI-based initiatives implemented in US and Canadian hospitals (diagnostic, predictive, administrative, clinical decision support) Objective 2 Quantitatively synthesize reported impacts on hospital efficiency (diagnosis time, resource allocation, cost reduction, workflow optimization) Objective 3 Quantitatively synthesize reported impacts on patient medical outcomes (mortality, readmission, complication rates, treatment success) Objective 4 Identify and systematically catalog challenges to AI integration into clinical workflows (generalisability, equity, ethics, privacy, provider resistance) Objective 5 Compare US and Canadian AI adoption patterns, priorities, and reported barriers Research questions (exact wording): RQ1: What are the main artificial intelligence-based initiatives that American and Canadian hospitals have implemented to improve their internal processes between September 2022 and August 2024? RQ2: How have these artificial intelligence-based initiatives impacted hospitals' performance (efficiency, resource allocation, clinical decision-making) and patients' medical outcomes (diagnostic accuracy, mortality, readmission, quality of life)? PICo framework: Component Definition Population (P) Hospitals located in the United States or Canada (all types: academic, tertiary, community, rural, teaching, for-profit, non-profit) Phenomenon of Interest (I) Artificial intelligence-based initiatives, including but not limited to: machine learning, deep learning, convolutional neural networks, natural language processing, large language models, generative AI, computer vision, clinical decision support systems, predictive analytics, robotic surgical systems, wearable-integrated AI, and administrative automation tools Context (Co) Hospital internal functioning, defined as clinical workflows (diagnosis, treatment, monitoring), administrative processes (scheduling, documentation, billing), resource allocation (staffing, bed management, equipment), and clinical decision-making pathways during the period September 1, 2022 to August 31, 2024 2. Background and Rationale Why US and Canada together? The United States and Canada share a geographic region and have highly interconnected healthcare research ecosystems, yet their healthcare systems differ fundamentally in financing (private insurance–dominant in US vs. single-payer in Canada), regulation (FDA vs. Health Canada), and AI governance approaches (Radu, 2021; Hummelsberger et al., 2023). Comparing these two countries allows the review to identify whether AI adoption patterns and impacts differ by healthcare system type—a question with implications for other countries considering national AI strategies. Why September 2022 to August 2024? This 24-month window was selected for three reasons. First, 2022 marked the peak year for US Food and Drug Administration approvals of AI- and machine learning-enabled medical devices, with more devices approved in 2022 than in any prior year (Joshi et al., 2024). Second, the rapid emergence of generative AI and large language models (e.g., GPT-3.5/4) in late 2022 fundamentally changed the landscape of clinical and administrative AI applications (Waisberg et al., 2023; Zaretsky et al., 2024). Third, a focused two-year window ensures the review captures the most current evidence, which is critical for a rapidly evolving technology field where studies older than 24–36 months may describe obsolete AI architectures. What is already known: prior systematic reviews Review Focus Key finding Gap this review addresses Meskó et al. (2018) mHealth Digital health transformation Identified medical imaging and decision support as primary AI domains Predates 2022 FDA approval surge; no US-Canada comparison Choudhury & Asan (2020) JMIR Med Inform AI safety in clinical settings Emphasized algorithmic bias and data quality risks Did not assess hospital internal functioning as outcome Obermeyer & Emanuel (2016) NEJM Big data and machine learning Identified potential for AI to exacerbate inequities Conceptual, not empirical synthesis Yin et al. (2021) J Med Internet Res AI in US hospitals Mapped early adoption patterns Single country; predates 2022–2024 LLM era What remains unknown (gap statement): No prior systematic review has: (1) simultaneously compared US and Canadian hospital AI implementations using a standardized methodology; (2) restricted to the post-2022 FDA approval peak period; (3) operationalized "hospital internal functioning" as a distinct outcome domain separate from patient outcomes; (4) applied GRADE certainty assessment to AI hospital implementation evidence; or (5) systematically cataloged implementation challenges (generalisability, equity, ethics, provider resistance) as a primary synthesis outcome rather than a secondary mention. Expected contribution: This review will produce the first systematically synthesized, GRADE-assessed evidence base on AI in US and Canadian hospitals for the 2022–2024 period, usable by hospital administrators, health technology assessment agencies (e.g., CADTH in Canada, ICER in the US), and policymakers developing national AI governance frameworks. 3. Methods Overview Study design: Systematic review following PRISMA 2020 guidelines (Page et al., 2021). No meta-analysis planned a priori due to anticipated heterogeneity; narrative synthesis using Synthesis Without Meta-Analysis (SWiM) framework (Campbell et al., 2020). Eligibility criteria (summary): Inclusion: Peer-reviewed publications, English/French, AI in hospitals, US or Canada, September 2022–August 2024, quantitative component Exclusion: Non-hospital settings, no quantitative analysis, unpublished/preprint, full text unavailable Information sources: PubMed (biomedical literature, primary tool) Scopus (broad interdisciplinary coverage) Google Scholar (comprehensive coverage, used alongside standard databases) Search date: September–October 2024 Outcome measures (extracted): Diagnostic accuracy (sensitivity, specificity, AUC, accuracy, F1-score) Time-based efficiency (diagnosis time, treatment delay, length of stay) Clinical decision metrics (treatment selection, resource allocation, triage accuracy) Patient outcomes (mortality, readmission, complication rates, functional status) Implementation barriers (generalisability, equity, ethics, privacy, cost, provider resistance) Risk of bias assessment: QUADAS-2 for diagnostic accuracy studies (10 expected) PROBAST for prediction model studies (9 expected) ROBINS-I for non-randomized intervention studies (9 expected) RoB 2 for randomized controlled trials (1 expected) Dual independent assessment by two reviewers; conflicts resolved by third reviewer Certainty assessment: GRADE framework (Guyatt et al., 2011) applied to each major finding Synthesis method: Narrative synthesis with studies grouped into outcome domains identified during data extraction (expected domains: case detection efficiency, clinical decision-making impact, integration challenges) 4. title: Towards a GPT-Based Lean Production Consultant for Manufacturing Optimization
authors: Christian S. Magnus; Moritz Venschott
abstract: The ever-present competition between industrial companies, both domestically and globally, puts manufacturing companies under constant pressure to optimize. Lean Manufacturing approaches have proven their worth in this environment and continue to hold great promise in the age of digitalization in Smart Factories. However, due to a lack of internal expertise and human resources, very few companies succeed in realizing the hidden potential across all processes. Additional expertise and human resources are often bought in from consultants. Generative Pre-Trained Transformers (GPTs) are a class of deep learning models that process and generate text using text-to-text conversational interfaces. They use large amounts of pre-existing text data to learn complex patterns, semantic relationships, and contextual nuances. Simple conversations with ChatGPT show that it already has some knowledge about Lean Manufacturing. Further investigations are necessary to check, if it is capable to help manufacturing companies with Value Stream Analyses, Line Balancing, etc. to create conversational systems that guide users through the necessary analyses and optimization steps. This paper presents the results of a study on the applicability of OpenAI`s ChatGPT-4 as a substitute for external consulting services in the described area. It shows exemplary use-cases in manufacturing, the structure and results of an experimental study, and the challenges to be solved when using ChatGPT-4 as Lean Manufacturing consultant.

title: Generative AI in second-language writing: a systematic review of learning, feedback, and literacy outcomes
authors: Kristian Burhan
abstract: The diffusion of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has challenged assumptions about how English L2 writing is taught, supported, and assessed. This systematic literature review synthesised peer-reviewed empirical evidence on generative AI in English L2 writing, focusing on pedagogical transformation, feedback and assessment, and academic literacy. Following PRISMA 2020, searches of Scopus, PubMed, and ScienceDirect identified 912 records. After duplicate removal and eligibility screening, 18 empirical studies published between 2023 and 2025 were included, although the search window covered 2020-2025. The eligible studies were appraised with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT 2018), with 14 meeting at least 4 of 5 criteria under the manuscript's descriptive appraisal rubric and four scoring 3.0-3.5; none was excluded solely on quality. Owing to substantial heterogeneity in designs and outcomes, findings were synthesised narratively and no quantitative meta-analysis was attempted. Evidence indicates that generative AI can improve surface-level accuracy, revision activity, and selected language or self-regulatory outcomes, while effects on higher-order rhetorical and critical competencies remain inconsistent. AI is most defensible as a teacher-guided complement, with continuing concerns about academic integrity, over-reliance, assessment validity, and equity. The review identifies priorities for longitudinal, multi-model, and multi-site research.

title: The AI Revolution in the Manufacturing Environment: A Comprehensive Analysis of Implementation, Impact, and Future Directions
authors: Komal Rahevar; Dhara Patel; Grishma Patel; Mukesh Kumar Patel; Dhananjay Meshram
abstract: The production industry is experiencing the most radical change ever since the invention of the assembly line due to the introduction of Artificial Intelligence (AI). Going beyond conventional automation, AI opens up cognitive possibilities whereby systems can learn on the data and respond to the changing environment and optimize complex tasks on their own. The article is a detailed investigation of the complex nature of AI in the contemporary manufacturing setting. It starts with the definition of the pillars of core technology in the industrial AI that are machine learning, computer vision and the new frontier of Generative AI and Physical AI. The article has then methodically explored the main application applications predictive maintenance, quality control, process optimization, supply chain resilience, human-robot collaboration, and generative design and presented the mechanisms and measurable advantages of each using real-world examples. This is followed by a critical analysis which discusses the major challenges that impede mass adoption which include lack of data infrastructure, talent and culture gap, complication of integration with existing systems, and the black box problem. By combining the findings of the recent industry whitepapers, scholarly work, and surveys across the globe, this article offers a four-pillar how-to guide to successful AI implementation, which focuses on strategic alignment, value-driven use cases, effective data governance, and workforce transformation. Lastly, it envisions the trends of the future such as the emergence of sovereign AI, maturity of context-aware robotics, and essential contribution of AI to enhancing sustainability. The conclusion is that the holistic and human-focused approach is more than just good but the key to manufacturers to reap the full potential of AI and gain a competitive edge in addition to surviving in the age of Industry 4.0.Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Smart Manufacturing, Predictive Maintenance, Quality Control, Supply Chain Optimization, Human-Robot Collaboration (HRC), Generative AI, Digital Twin, Industry 4.0, Implementation Framework, Data Governance, Workforce Upskilling.

title: Aplicación de Inteligencia Artificial Generativa y Verificación Formal en el Descubrimiento de Microservicios
authors: D Devia Narváez; Nicolás Battaglia; Alejandro Fernández; Gustavo H. Rossi
abstract: El diseño de microservicios a partir de requisitos textuales constituye un desafío persisten te en la ingeniería de software, debido a la ambigüedad del lenguaje natural y a la ausencia de mecanismos formales que garanticen calidad arquitectónica. En el marco de una investigación doctoral en la Universidad Abierta Interamericana (UAI), se presenta ArchiGenMS, un pipeline evolutivo que combina modelos de lenguaje generativos (LLMs) con verificación formal en Lean para el descubrimiento automático de microservicios. La propuesta integra prompt engineering evolutivo, métricas estructurales de cohesión, granularidad y acoplamiento, y validación automática de restricciones arquitectónicas. Los experimentos realizados con datasets públicos de historias de usuario, como el caso g24-unibath, muestran que el enfoque permite generar arquitecturas con alta cohesión (LCOMavg = 0.167), granularidad controlada (SGMmax = 4) y bajo acoplamiento (Couplingmax = 1). Los resultados evidencian el potencial de integrar técnicas generativas y verificación formal para construir arquitecturas mantenibles y reproducibles en escenarios greenfield.

title: Generative artificial intelligence-powered approach to multiple criteria selection of advertising 4.0 services suppliers: case of sustainable fashion industry
authors: Shahryar Sorooshian; Syed Radzi Rahamaddulla; Mohd Hanafiah Ahmad
source_name: Journal of Fashion Marketing and Management
abstract: Purpose On both digital capability and sustainability, advertising 4.0 service providers are pivotal for brands that compete. However, choosing the right partner requires a structured, data-driven approach. The purpose of this article is to propose a novel approach to assist sustainable fashion businesses in selecting the best advertising 4.0 services suppliers. Design/methodology/approach The study proposed a multi-step approach that included artificial intelligence (AI) -generated insights as well as expert validation. Generative AI developed the initial decision criteria, which served as a comprehensive and advanced starting point. These criteria were refined through expert focus groups to ensure their comprehensiveness and applicability. A multi-criteria decision-making technique, ordinal priority approach (OPA), utilized to rank the existing service providers. To validate the proposed approach and identify the best advertising 4.0 provider, we went through every step of the model and successfully ranked alternative advertising service suppliers in a fashion industry case study. Findings A user-friendly advertising 4.0 provider selection model was developed for the fashion industry with a sustainability competitive advantage, including Twenty-two comprehensive criteria for market knowledge, sustainability practices, and technical competence. Among the alternative service suppliers obtainable by the case company, this study revealed alternative 2 as the best-match advertising 4.0 partner. As a result of this case study applicability validation, the proposed framework is potentially beneficial for all industries, mainly the fashion sector, because it enables them to make informed decisions that are consistent with their strategic goals. Originality/value This article is among the pioneers to integrate artificial intelligence for criteria generation with expert validation and OPA optimization, producing a replicable generative AI-assisted MCDM framework. It promotes the concept of advertising 4.0 and contributes to the literature on service supplier selection, particularly in the sustainable fashion sector.

title: From practice to pedagogy: A model of praxis-focused creative arts assessment in initial teacher education
authors: Katie Burke; David Roy; William Baker; Sian Chapman; Katie Hotko; Amy Hamilton
source_name: Arts and Humanities in Higher Education
abstract: In response to the growing need for authentic, pedagogically sound assessment in Initial Teacher Education (ITE), this study presents a model of praxis-focused Creative Arts assessment designed to integrate arts-making, critical reflection, and pedagogical theorising. Drawing on a multi-site, collaborative autoethnographic study involving six Australian universities, the research uses document analysis and thematic analysis of student survey data to identify critical characteristics that underpin effective praxis-focused assessment: meaningful context, embodied arts engagement, and critical reflection, which collectively contribute to theory-practice integration. The study results in a theoretically grounded and empirically supported model of praxis-focused assessment that is affirmed as a pedagogical tool for preparing confident, competent arts educators. The model offers a framework for assessment in Creative Arts ITE, enhancing student engagement and classroom readiness while addressing contemporary challenges such as generative AI and online learning.

title: LLM-Guided Exemplar Selection for Few-Shot Wearable-Sensor Human Activity Recognition
authors: Elsen Ronando; Sozo Inoue
abstract: In this paper, we propose an LLM-Guided Exemplar Selection framework to address a key limitation in state-of-the-art Human Activity Recognition (HAR) methods: their reliance on large labeled datasets and purely geometric exemplar selection, which often fail to distinguish similar wearable sensor activities such as walking, walking upstairs, and walking downstairs. Our method incorporates semantic reasoning via an LLM-generated knowledge prior that captures feature importance, inter-class confusability, and exemplar budget multipliers, and uses it to guide exemplar scoring and selection. These priors are combined with margin-based validation cues, PageRank centrality, hubness penalization, and facility-location optimization to obtain a compact and informative set of exemplars. Evaluated on the UCI-HAR dataset under strict few-shot conditions, the framework achieves a macro F1-score of 88.78%, outperforming classical approaches such as random sampling, herding, and k-center. The results show that LLM-derived semantic priors, when integrated with structural and geometric cues, provide a stronger foundation for selecting representative sensor exemplars in few-shot wearable-sensor HAR.

title: Scale-Up Interconnect Technology in AI Clusters: Architecture Evolution, Performance Analysis, and Development Trends
authors: Yanling Chen; Xinxin Wang; Yang Yang
source_name: International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
abstract: With the explosive growth of trillion-parameter large language models, GPU cluster scale-up interconnect technology has emerged as a critical bottleneck limiting the efficiency of distributed training. Its performance optimization and systemlevel innovation directly determine the effective utilization of large-scale computing resources in modern AI workloads. This paper systematically reviews the evolutionary trajectory and industry landscape of scale-up interconnect technologies for AI clusters. Starting from the fundamental technological driving forces, we first analyze the extreme requirements for ultra-low latency and ultra-high bandwidth imposed by the high-frequency, large-volume communication patterns inherent in tensor parallelism (TP). Building on this analysis, we conduct an in-depth comparison of architectural designs and performance trade-offs across different technological routes, including NVIDIA's proprietary solutions and open alternatives such as RDMAintegrated interconnects, memory-semantic Ethernet, and PCIebased fabrics. In addition, the role of scenario-specific innovations is examined through representative examples such as Tesla's System-on-Wafer (SoW) architecture and the TTP/TTPoE protocol stack. Our analysis indicates that AI cluster scale-up interconnect technologies are evolving toward a pattern in which proprietary solutions dominate ultra-large-scale deployments, open standards gain advantages through ecosystem scalability, and optical interconnects progressively overcome physical limitations. Looking forward, performance breakthroughs, convergence toward open standards, and deep integration across heterogeneous technologies are expected to define the core development trends of next-generation interconnect systems. This work provides both theoretical insights and practical guidance for interconnect technology selection in ultra-large-scale AI clusters, as well as for the design of future high-performance interconnect architectures.

title: Review of Active Distribution Network Planning: Elements in Optimization Models and Generative AI Applications
authors: Antonio E. Saldaña-González; Mònica Aragüés‐Peñalba; Vinicius Gadelha; Andreas Sumper
abstract: Active distribution networks (ADNs) are rapidly evolving with the integration of distributed energy resources, flexible loads, and energy storage systems. Traditional planning methods, based on passive upgrades and worst-case scenarios, are no longer adequate for high DER penetration and dynamic system behavior. This review highlights the key evolution needs that will drive the evolution towards a more dynamic and optimized active distribution planning. Furthermore, this work reviews the core elements in ADN planning, covering time horizons, objectives, decision variables, uncertainty approaches, and optimal power flow formulations. This work also reviews recent generative AI models applied to active distribution networks, presenting a structured classification and definitions of each generative AI category.

title: Analyzing Vulnerability Through Narratives: A Prompt-Based NLP Framework for Information Extraction and Insight Generation
authors: Aswathi Padmavilochanan; Veena Gangadharan; Tarek Rashed; Amritha Natarajan
abstract: This interdisciplinary pilot study examines the use of Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques, specifically Large Language Models (LLMs) with Prompt Engineering (PE), to analyze economic vulnerability from qualitative self-narratives. Seventy narratives from twenty-five women in the Palk Bay coastal region of Rameshwaram, India were analyzed using a schema adapted from a contextual empowerment framework. The study operationalizes theoretical constructs into structured Information Extraction (IE) templates, enabling systematic identification of multiple vulnerability aspects, contributing factors, and experiential expressions. Prompt templates were iteratively refined and validated through dual-annotator review, achieving an F1-score of 0.78 on a held-out subset. Extracted elements were examined through downstream analysis, including pattern grouping and graph-based visualization, to reveal co-occurrence structures and recurring vulnerability configurations across narratives. The findings demonstrate that LLMs, when aligned with domain-specific conceptual models and supported by human-in-the-loop validation, can enable interpretable and replicable analysis of self-narratives. While findings are bounded by the pilot scale and community-specific context, the approach supports translation of narrative evidence into community-level program design and targeted grassroots outreach, with planned expansion to multi-site, multilingual datasets for broader applicability.

title: Towards Trustworthy Autonomous Logistics Through AI Assurance, Security, and Explainability Frameworks
authors: Duggirala Aravind; Suzan Fouad Bakr; N. V. Suresh
source_name: Advances in computational intelligence and robotics book series
abstract: Combination of Generative AI, Digital Twins and autonomous operations are accelerating the rate of evolution in the logistics field. The technologies are transforming the supply chain planning, coordination, and response to dynamic market conditions. Chapter analyses the importance of AI-based automation in making predictive decisions, real-time optimization and smart coordination within logistics networks. Meanwhile, it considers the most important issues of reliability, security, and transparency in more autonomous systems. The discussion throws light on the efficiency of the predictive algorithms, robotics, and digital replicas in enhancing efficiency. The chapter integrates the findings of the emerging research and industry case studies to come up with the framework of creating trustful and robust logistics ecosystems. The research comes to the conclusion that the future of logistics is not only about the technological innovation but also about the responsible government, transparency, and constant learning in intelligent systems.

title: Intelligent Human-Machine Partnership for Manufacturing: Enhancing Warehouse Planning through Simulation-Driven Knowledge Graphs and LLM Collaboration
authors: Himabindu Thogaru; Saisubramaniam Gopalakrishnan; Zishan Ahmad; Anirudh Deodhar
abstract: Manufacturing planners face complex operational challenges that require seamless collaboration between human expertise and intelligent systems to achieve optimal performance in modern production environments. Traditional approaches to analyzing simulation-based manufacturing data often create barriers between human decision-makers and critical operational insights, limiting effective partnership in manufacturing planning. Our framework establishes a collaborative intelligence system integrating Knowledge Graphs and Large Language Model-based agents to bridge this gap, empowering manufacturing professionals through natural language interfaces for complex operational analysis. The system transforms simulation data into semantically rich representations, enabling planners to interact naturally with operational insights without specialized expertise. A collaborative LLM agent works alongside human decision-makers, employing iterative reasoning that mirrors human analytical thinking while generating precise queries for knowledge extraction and providing transparent validation. This partnership approach to manufacturing bottleneck identification, validated through operational scenarios, demonstrates enhanced performance while maintaining human oversight and decision authority. For operational inquiries, the system achieves near-perfect accuracy through natural language interaction. For investigative scenarios requiring collaborative analysis, we demonstrate the framework's effectiveness in supporting human experts to uncover interconnected operational issues that enhance understanding and decision-making. This work advances collaborative manufacturing by creating intuitive methods for actionable insights, reducing cognitive load while amplifying human analytical capabilities in evolving manufacturing ecosystems.

title: PHENO-RAG: An artificial intelligence tool for guideline-informed management decisions in hepatocellular carcinoma
authors: Ciro Celsa; Mauro Giuffrè; Gabriele Di Maria; Salvatore Gruttadauria; Ugo Palazzo; Roberto Miraglia; Luigi Maruzzelli; Duilio Pagano; Roberto Cannella; Federico Midiri; Roberta Ciccia; M.
